articles.title: Que dia é a Black Friday 2026 no Brasil? Veja data e dicas do g1 | G1
articles.standfirst: A Black Friday 2026 já tem data confirmada. Descubra quando acontece o evento, tendências de consumo e como se blindar da 'Black Fraude'.
articles.summary: Confira a data da Black Friday 2026 e aprenda a usar ferramentas de IA e monitoramento de preços para garantir descontos reais e evitar golpes no evento.
articles.body:
A edição de 2026 da Black Friday já tem data marcada no calendário do comércio brasileiro: o evento acontecerá nesta sexta-feira, dia 27 de novembro, mantendo a tradição da última sexta-feira do mês.

O Guia de Compras está mostrando, a cada dia útil, como estão os preços de 74 produtos monitorados pelo g1 desde agosto.

A ideia é ajudar o leitor a saber se o desconto é real ou se as lojas aumentaram o preço para anunciar promoção depois, a famosa “metade do dobro”.

Amelhor arma do consumidor para garantir descontos legítimos é a preparação e planejamento. Para não cair em ciladas , a primeira dica é começar a acompanhar o preço dos produtos quanto antes.

A Black Friday 2026 acontece durante todo o dia de 27 de novembro, última sexta-feira do mês.

O comportamento do consumidor para 2026: IA e listas prontas

A postura dos compradores está cada vez mais estratégica. De acordo com um levantamento realizado pelo Google no último mês de agosto:

48% dos clientes afirmam que pretendem chegar à data com uma lista fechada do que precisam comprar;

41% dos consumidores planejam investir um valor maior do que no ano anterior;

60% dos entrevistados encaram o evento como a principal (ou única) oportunidade do ano para adquirir produtos de alto valor agregado ;

15% já utilizam ferramentas de inteligência artificial ativamente para rastrear preços, comparar histórico de valores e avaliar se a oferta é vantajosa.

Para não ser vítima da famosa tática de comprar "pela metade do dobro", especialistas e órgãos de defesa do consumidor, como o Procon-SP, reforçam que o monitoramento deve começar semanas antes.

Como não existe tabelamento de valores no Brasil, a única forma de saber se uma promoção é real é conhecendo a média de preço praticada nos meses anteriores.

Caso você flagre aumentos maquiados seguidos de falsas reduções, registre capturas de tela (prints) com data e hora para denunciar ao Procon.

Controle o impulso e desconfie de promoções muito boas

Fazer uma lista de compras combinadas (Black Friday + presentes de Natal) é uma boa tática para se manter no orçamento.

Promoção boa demais em site desconhecido também é motivo de alerta. Antes de inserir seus dados:

Consulte a página da loja em plataformas como Reclame Aqui e Consumidor.gov.br;

Verifique se o site exibe claramente CNPJ, razão social, endereço físico e canais oficiais de atendimento;

Desconfie de páginas que só aceitam pagamento via Pix ou boleto com desconto muito fora da realidade.

articles.title: Padrasto é preso por morte de jovem carbonizado em São Gonçalo | G1
articles.standfirst: Corpo de Marllon Galdino dos Santos, de 19 anos, foi encontrado carbonizado dentro de um carro, no domingo (22). Os investigadores encontraram indícios de sangue no carro do padrasto e imagens dele comprando gasolina.
articles.summary: Padrasto preso em São Gonçalo é suspeito de matar Marllon Galdino por vingança contra a ex-mulher; polícia encontrou sangue e imagens de compra de gasolina.
articles.body:
Marcelo comprando combustível no dia do crime — Foto: Reprodução

A Delegacia de Homicídios de Homicídios de Niterói, São Gonçalo e Itaboraí prendeu na noite desta segunda-feira (23) o padrasto de Marllon Galdino dos Santos, assassinado depois de sair para ir a uma festa em São Gonçalo, na Região Metropolitana do Rio.

Segundo a polícia, Marcelo David da Costa, de 50 anos, é suspeito de envolvimento com o assassinato e foi preso por fraude processual.

O corpo de Marllon, de 19 anos, foi encontrado carbonizado dentro de um carro , às margens da BR-101, no bairro Gradim, neste domingo (22). Segundo Pedro Henrique Neves, delegado-assistente da DH Niterói, os investigadores encontraram indícios de sangue no carro do padrastro e imagens dele comprando gasolina.

Segundo a investigação, Marcelo limpou os bancos do carro, e se desfez do galão de combustível, mas a perícia da DH encontrou os vestígios de sangue quando jogou luminol no veículo. Neves explicou que vai pedir à Justiça a prisão temporária do padrasto.

De acordo coma investigação, Marrlon foi morto com pancadas na cabeça, antes de ter seu corpo carbonizado. A polícia ainda investiga se Marcelo agiu sozinho.

Um dos possíveis motivos investigados pela polícia para o crime é que o preso queria se vingar da mãe de Marllon. Marcelo foi casado com a mãe do rapaz por mais de dez anos. Eles se separaram em outubro deste ano. Não houve relatos de violência doméstica contra ela, mas a mulher sofreu ameaças.

Marllon trabalhava como auxiliar de serviços gerais em um hotel no Leme, na Zona Sul do Rio, e morava no bairro Porto Novo. Na noite de sábado (21), ele saiu de casa para ir a uma festa na casa de um amigo, no Jardim Catarina, mas não chegou ao destino.

A família também desconfia que outra pessoa tenha usado o celular do jovem para trocar mensagens com parentes naquela noite. O jeito de escrever e as palavras utilizadas nas conversas chamaram a atenção dos familiares.

Corpo de Marllon Galdino dos Santos foi encontrado carbonizado em São Gonçalo, no RJ — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

Em uma das mensagens, enviada à mãe por volta da meia-noite de domingo, o celular de Marllon recebeu o seguinte texto: "Maior furada. Acho que caí numa braba. É assalto. Acho que vou perder tudo."

Um parente do jovem, que conversou com a equipe de reportagem e pediu para não ser identificado, contou que a família começou a procurar informações com amigos depois de receber as mensagens.

"Em torno de meia-noite mandou algumas mensagens estranhas dizendo que tava num local achando que ia ser assaltado, que ia perder tudo. Então, a partir dessa mensagem, a gente já começou a perguntar aos amigos o que tinha acontecido, se ele tinha chegado na festa, e aí informaram que ele não tinha chegado."

Polícia investiga se grupo se passou por jovem antes de ele ser encontrado morto em São Gonçalo — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Globo

articles.title: Empresa abre 140 vagas temporários para Black Friday na Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Oportunidades são para as lojas dos Barris e Paralela, em Salvador, e no Centro de Distribuição, em Simões Filho. Ao todo, rede oferece mais de 500 postos em cinco estados.
articles.summary: Oportunidades são para as lojas dos Barris e Paralela, e no Centro de Distribuição, em Simões Filho. Ao todo, rede oferece mais de 500 postos em cinco estados.
articles.body:
Ferreira Costa abre 140 vagas temporárias para Black Friday 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

O home center Ferreira Costa abriu 140 vagas temporárias na Bahia durante o período pré-Black Friday. As oportunidades estão distribuídas entre as lojas dos Barris e Paralela, em Salvador , e no Centro de Distribuição, em Simões Filho , na região metropolitana da capital.

Ao todo, a empresa disponibilizou mais de 500 postos de trabalho nos cinco estados do Nordeste onde atua.

As oportunidades são para funções como auxiliar de logística, separador, auxiliar de e-commerce, conferente, caixa, apoio de caixa, prevenção de perdas, atendimento e Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor (SAC). Além dessas, estão previstas também vagas afirmativas para pessoas com deficiência e profissionais com 45 anos ou mais.

Os interessados por uma oportunidade podem se cadastrar no site de Carreiras da Ferreira Costa . As contratações buscam atender o aumento da demanda nas lojas físicas, nos canais digitais e nas operações de logística durante a campanha.

A contratação temporária também pode resultar em efetivação. A empresa afirma que mantém uma taxa média de retenção de aproximadamente 70% dos profissionais sazonais, que podem ser aproveitados em vagas permanentes após o período de maior movimento.

Para este ano, o home center projeta um crescimento de 25% no número de pedidos em comparação com a campanha da Black Friday do ano de 2025.

articles.title: Fiscalização encontra trabalho infantil em 113 empresas e afasta 179 adolescentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho identificou irregularidades em quase 80% dos estabelecimentos inspecionados em cinco estados. Ao todo, 124 máquinas e equipamentos foram interditados.
articles.summary: Fiscalização identificou irregularidades em quase 80% dos estabelecimentos inspecionados em cinco estados. Ao todo, 124 máquinas e equipamentos foram interditados.
articles.body:
Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho identificou 113 empresas com adolescentes em situação de trabalho infantil em cinco estados brasileiros. — Foto: Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho

Uma operação da Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, vinculada à Secretaria de Inspeção do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE), identificou adolescentes trabalhando em atividades perigosas em 113 empresas de cinco estados brasileiros.

Segundo a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, 179 adolescentes com idades entre 13 e 17 anos foram afastados dessas atividades após a identificação das irregularidades.

A fiscalização foi realizada em novembro, em 56 municípios de Goiás, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Santa Catarina e São Paulo. Ao todo, os auditores inspecionaram 142 empresas dos setores de tecelagem e comércio de carnes, incluindo açougues e supermercados.

O trabalho infantil foi identificado em quase 80% dos estabelecimentos fiscalizados. Além disso, 124 máquinas e equipamentos foram interditados em 60 empresas por apresentarem risco grave e iminente de acidentes.

Segundo a Coordenadora do Grupo Especial Móvel de Fiscalização do Trabalho Infantil Paula Neves, as situações encontradas demonstram que a utilização de adolescentes em atividades perigosas não é um fato isolado.

"O que constatamos nos estados fiscalizados não foram situações isoladas, mas a utilização recorrente de adolescentes em atividades enquadradas entre as piores formas de trabalho infantil, expostos a risco grave de acidente de trabalho e submetidos a agentes físicos, químicos e biológicos prejudiciais ao seu estágio de desenvolvimento”, afirmou.

Adolescentes operavam máquinas perigosas

Segundo a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, 179 adolescentes foram afastados das atividades após a identificação das irregularidades. — Foto: Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho

Nos açougues e supermercados, os fiscais encontraram adolescentes cortando e desossando carnes, operando serras e moedores, utilizando facas profissionais e entrando em câmaras frigoríficas.

Os fiscais também encontraram adolescentes em contato direto com sangue, vísceras e resíduos de animais.

Em Santa Catarina, onde a fiscalização se concentrou nas tecelagens, adolescentes operavam máquinas industriais e transportavam sacos de algodão de até 35 quilos.

🔎 Segundo a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, essas atividades são consideradas algumas das piores formas de trabalho infantil pela legislação brasileira, por colocarem em risco a saúde e a segurança dos adolescentes. Elas fazem parte da Lista das Piores Formas de Trabalho Infantil (Lista TIP), criada por decreto em 2008, que inclui o uso de máquinas perigosas, a exposição a produtos químicos e outras condições prejudiciais à saúde.

O coordenador-geral de Fiscalização em Segurança e Saúde no Trabalho da Secretaria de Inspeção do Trabalho, Fabiano Rizzo Carvalho, destacou a quantidade de interdições realizadas durante o operativo.

“Diversas máquinas estavam funcionando sem dispositivos de segurança exigidos pela NR-12, sobretudo a serra-fita. Dos 60 estabelecimentos com interdições, 55 deles tiveram esse tipo de máquina paralisado. As atividades tiveram de ser interrompidas em razão da exposição de trabalhadores a riscos graves e iminentes de amputações, esmagamentos, aprisionamentos, lacerações e outros acidentes graves”, ressaltou.

Além do trabalho infantil, os auditores identificaram máquinas e equipamentos sem os dispositivos de segurança obrigatórios, incluindo serras, moedores, amaciadores, processadores e máquinas industriais de tecelagem.

Em alguns estabelecimentos, trabalhadores precisavam empurrar pedaços de carne em direção a lâminas em movimento, sem a proteção adequada.

Segundo o MTE, 55 dos 60 estabelecimentos com máquinas interditadas utilizavam serras para cortar carne sem cumprir as exigências de segurança.

São Paulo teve o maior número de adolescentes afastados, enquanto Minas Gerais registrou trabalho infantil em todas as empresas fiscalizadas.

São Paulo concentrou o maior número de adolescentes afastados — Foto: Arte g1

Em Goiás, 32% dos adolescentes encontrados durante a fiscalização estavam fora da escola.

No Paraná, os auditores encontraram um adolescente de apenas 13 anos trabalhando como repositor, sem registro.

Em Minas Gerais, os fiscais encontraram adolescentes de até 15 anos trabalhando como açougueiros, operando serras para cortar ossos e utilizando facas profissionais.

Fiscalização da Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho ocorreu em 56 municípios — Foto: Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho

No Brasil, menores de 16 anos não podem trabalhar , exceto como aprendizes, a partir dos 14 anos.

🔎 Adolescentes de 16 e 17 anos podem trabalhar, mas não podem exercer atividades perigosas, insalubres ou que coloquem em risco sua saúde, segurança e desenvolvimento.

Segundo a Auditoria-Fiscal do Trabalho, foi determinado o afastamento imediato dos menores de 16 anos encontrados em situação irregular. Já os adolescentes de 16 e 17 anos deverão ser transferidos para atividades permitidas por lei, conforme orientação aos empregadores.

As empresas onde foi identificado trabalho infantil serão autuadas. Os adolescentes que tiveram seus contratos encerrados deverão receber as verbas rescisórias a que têm direito.

O MTE informou ainda que os jovens serão encaminhados à rede de proteção à infância e à adolescência, com acesso a serviços de assistência social, saúde e educação.

articles.title: Exposição gratuita em SP reúne bastidores de 'Carandiru' e de outros filmes de Hector Babenco, diretor que marcou o cinema brasileiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Mostra no Itaú Cultural apresenta fotografias, documentos, objetos pessoais e materiais inéditos da carreira do cineasta, que também dirigiu 'Pixote' e 'O beijo da mulher aranha'; visitação vai até fevereiro de 2027.
articles.summary: Mostra no Itaú Cultural apresenta fotografias, documentos, objetos pessoais e materiais inéditos da carreira do cineasta, que também dirigiu 'Pixote' e 'O beijo da mulher aranha'; visitação vai até fevereiro de 2027.
articles.body:
Hector Babenco na gravação do filme Carandiru, de 2003. — Foto: Divulgação/AcervoHBFilmes

O filme Carandiru (2003), de Hector Babenco, levou ao cinema histórias de presos da antiga Casa de Detenção de São Paulo, na Zona Norte da capital, a partir do livro Estação Carandiru, do médico Drauzio Varella . Os bastidores dessa e de outras produções do cineasta estão entre os destaques de uma exposição gratuita no Itaú Cultural, na Avenida Paulista, que abriu ao público na semana passada.

Batizada de "Ocupação Hector Babenco", a mostra reúne fotografias, documentos, materiais de produção, poemas inéditos e objetos pessoais do diretor, que também assina filmes como Pixote, a lei do mais fraco (1980) e O beijo da mulher aranha (1985). A exposição fica em cartaz até 14 de fevereiro de 2027.

Nascido em Buenos Aires, na Argentina, Babenco chegou a São Paulo em 1969 e se naturalizou brasileiro no ano seguinte. Ele morreu em 2016, aos 70 anos . Ao longo da carreira, construiu uma filmografia marcada por histórias de personagens marginalizados e por temas como violência, desigualdade social e conflitos humanos.

O percurso da exposição não segue uma ordem cronológica e é dividido em três núcleos. O primeiro reúne filmes realizados no Brasil, nos Estados Unidos e na Argentina, além de registros de sua experiência como diretor teatral.

O segundo apresenta duas obras mais pessoais do cineasta: Coração iluminado (1998) e Meu amigo hindu (2015), inspiradas em episódios de sua própria vida.

Já o terceiro concentra quatro dos títulos mais conhecidos de sua carreira: Lúcio Flávio, o passageiro da agonia (1977), Pixote, a lei do mais fraco (1980), O beijo da mulher aranha (1985) e Carandiru (2003).

Entre os objetos pessoais expostos estão uma agenda, uma caixa de charutos, lupas e a pelúcia de um macaquinho utilizada em Meu amigo hindu, último longa-metragem dirigido por Babenco. A mostra também apresenta materiais inéditos dos bastidores de algumas produções e poemas do cineasta.

Ao entrar na exposição, o visitante recebe um livreto com 14 perguntas e respostas que funciona como guia da visitação e traz curiosidades sobre os filmes e os processos de criação do diretor.

A homenagem também inclui uma retrospectiva cinematográfica, com exibições presenciais no teatro do Itaú Cultural e filmes disponíveis gratuitamente na plataforma Itaú Cultural Play.

As sessões presenciais acontecem nos dias 27, 28 e 29 de novembro, sempre às 16h e às 19h.

Na sexta-feira (27), entram em cartaz o documentário Babenco – alguém tem que ouvir o coração e dizer: parou (2019), dirigido por Bárbara Paz, e Pixote, a lei do mais fraco (1980).

No sábado (28), serão exibidos Coração iluminado (1998) e Brincando nos campos do Senhor (1991). Já no domingo (29), a programação terá O passado (2007) e Ironweed (1987), primeiro filme de Babenco realizado em Hollywood, estrelado por Jack Nicholson e Meryl Streep.

Na Itaú Cultural Play, a retrospectiva reúne oito longas-metragens dirigidos pelo cineasta e o documentário de Bárbara Paz. Os títulos ficam disponíveis até 16 de maio de 2028, com exceção de O passado, que poderá ser assistido até 14 de fevereiro de 2027.

Nascido em 7 de fevereiro de 1946, em Buenos Aires, Hector Babenco chegou ao Brasil em 1969 e construiu aqui grande parte de sua carreira. Seu reconhecimento internacional ganhou força com O beijo da mulher aranha (1985), estrelado por William Hurt, Raúl Juliá e Sônia Braga. O longa recebeu quatro indicações ao Oscar de 1986, incluindo melhor filme e melhor direção. William Hurt venceu como melhor ator.

Em Pixote, a lei do mais fraco, o diretor retratou crianças e adolescentes em situação de vulnerabilidade e submetidos à violência institucional. Já Carandiru, adaptação do livro de Drauzio Varella, abordou o cotidiano dos detentos do presídio paulistano antes do massacre de 1992.

📍 Onde? Itaú Cultural – Avenida Paulista, 149, Bela Vista, região central de São Paulo.

📅 Quando? de terça-feira a sábado, das 11h às 20h; domingos e feriados, das 11h às 19h. Até o dia 14 de fevereiro de 2027.

📍 Onde? Teatro do Itaú Cultural, de 27 a 29 de novembro. Sessões às 16h e às 19h.

articles.title: Justiça da Espanha concede anistia a líder separatista catalão | G1
articles.standfirst: Tribunal Supremo espanhol aplicou a lei de anistia a Puigdemont, processado por tentativa fracassada de separar a Catalunha do restante da Espanha em 2017. Decisão abre caminho para líder separatista retornar ao país ibérico.
articles.summary: Tribunal Supremo espanhol aplicou a lei de anistia a Puigdemont, processado por tentativa fracassada de separar a Catalunha do restante da Espanha em 2017. Decisão abre caminho para líder separatista retornar ao país ibérico.
articles.body:
Carles Puigdemont faz sinal de resistência em foto de 2024, quando ele compareceu para fazer um discurso para apoiadores em Barcelona e depois, fugiu de novo. — Foto: Lorena Sopena/Reuters

O Tribunal Supremo espanhol aplicou a lei de anistia ao líder independentista catalão Carles Puigdemont e encerrou o processo por sua implicação na tentativa fracassada de secessão dessa região espanhola em 2017, o que lhe permite voltar livremente ao país nove anos depois.

"Declara-se o arquivamento definitivo dos fatos (...), por extinção da eventual responsabilidade penal por anistia de D. Carles Puigdemont ", indicou a decisão divulgada nesta segunda-feira (23), e que representa a última etapa da aplicação da polêmica lei aprovada pelo Parlamento espanhol em 2024.

A decisão foi divulgada a menos de uma semana das eleições gerais de 29 de novembro na Espanha e após uma legislatura marcada, entre outros fatores, pela aprovação da lei de anistia.

A polêmica norma foi a moeda de troca paga pelo primeiro-ministro socialista Pedro Sánchez para se reeleger no fim de 2023, graças, entre outros, ao apoio necessário dos partidos independentistas catalães, incluindo o Juntos pela Catalunha , de Puigdemont.

Embora o Parlamento espanhol tenha aprovado a lei há dois anos, Puigdemont e outros líderes independentistas ainda não haviam se beneficiado dela porque o Tribunal Supremo decidiu que a legislação não era aplicável aos investigados por crime de desvio de fundos.

Mas o Tribunal Constitucional, ao qual os afetados haviam recorrido, a validou em outubro e, pouco depois, o Supremo revogou as ordens de prisão contra o separatista.

articles.title: Jensen Huang volta ao comando da Nvidia após intervenção de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: O retorno de Huang teve efeito imediato no preço das ações da maior empresa de chips do mundo. Em um minuto, a Nvidia ganhou US$ 1 trilhão em valor de mercado.
articles.summary: Jensen Huang reassumiu a Nvidia após Donald Trump intervir no conselho da empresa, gerando valorização recorde das ações e polêmica sobre segurança nacional.
articles.body:
Com o envolvimento direto do presidente Donald Trump , a disputa pelo comando da maior empresa de chips do mundo teve uma reviravolta. O chefe da Nvidia , Jensen Huang, voltou ao cargo 11 dias depois de ter renunciado. Huang teve um caso extraconjugal com uma mulher acusada de ser espiã da China .

Ele está de volta e prometeu ser um CEO melhor. Essa reviravolta pegou milhares de pessoas de surpresa. Mas a Casa Branca, nem tanto. Donald Trump interveio pessoalmente na decisão da Nvidia, tomada durante o fim de semana. Em uma entrevista ao canal americano CNBC, disse que negociou a volta do CEO com o conselho executivo da empresa:

"Eu convenci os diretores. Fui eu que fechei o acordo. Uma das coisas que o conselho queria saber era se teria algum problema de segurança nacional. Então, nós contamos tudo o que sabemos, demos nossa garantia”, afirmou o presidente.

Nas redes sociais, Trump celebrou e publicou uma foto editada em que Huang aparece no lugar dele no dia em que Trump foi alvo de um tiro de raspão, em um comício em 2024.

Segundo o comunicado da Nvidia, o conselho executivo votou de forma unânime pela volta do CEO. O conselho afirmou que ficou satisfeito com a “franqueza” de Jensen Huang, que recebeu informações do alto escalão do governo e que estava “confiante de que o retorno dele não representa qualquer risco à segurança nacional”.

Reviravolta: conselho da Nvidia devolve o comando da empresa a Jensen Huang — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Nesta segunda-feira (23), o jornal “The New York Times” publicou que a chinesa no centro desse escândalo, Alice Huang, manteve contato com uma autoridade da principal agência de espionagem da China por mais de um ano, enquanto tinha um caso com o chefe da Nvidia. Ela também era casada e o marido e sócio dela, Kang Wei, trabalhava para a mesma agência de espionagem, segundo informações da inteligência americana obtidas pela reportagem.

Alice Huang era executiva da MegaSpeed, uma empresa de Singapura que comprava chips da Nvidia. Os investigadores americanos apuram se ela contrabandeou chips para a China e se a companhia prestava serviços de computação para empresas chinesas.

O retorno de Jensen Huang ao comando da Nvidia teve efeito imediato no preço das ações da empresa. Em um minuto, ela ganhou US$ 1 trilhão em valor de mercado - as ações subiram 30% e levaram nas costas os principais índices das bolsas americanas. O da Nasdaq subiu mais de 6% nesta segunda-feira (23).

Um gestor de investimentos avalia que o mercado reagiu bem porque era difícil achar um substituto para Jensen Huang - que fundou a Nvidia, tem 33 anos à frente da empresa e, por isso, tem também uma visão única sobre o negócio.

Quem também pode ter se beneficiado com a disparada é o presidente americano. No final de 2025, Trump tinha investido mais de US$ 12 milhões em ações da Nvidia, segundo o relatório de divulgação financeira da presidência. Parlamentares do partido do próprio presidente condenaram a intervenção direta de Trump no caso. O deputado republicano Don Bacon disse:

"Jensen Huang foi comprometido e explorado por uma espiã chinesa. A Nvidia deveria ter seguido em frente sem Huang e ignorado o desejo inexplicável do governo de salvá-lo”.

Deputados e senadores agora querem investigar não só se a Nvidia e Jensen Huang violaram restrições à venda de chips e comprometeram a segurança nacional, mas também se o governo agiu para favorecer os negócios do CEO.

O abastecimento de água será interrompido em mais de 40 localidades de São Luís, a partir das 5h desta quinta-feira (26), para a realização de serviços de manutenção preventiva e corretiva no Sistema Italuís. De acordo com a Caema, 200 bairros da capital maranhense atendidos por sistemas de poços e pelo Sistema Sacavém não terão o fornecimento de água interrompido.

articles.title: Justiça manda Energisa religar luz de parques em Cuiabá | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão prevê multa diária de R$ 30 mil e proíbe novos cortes que atinjam serviços essenciais. Desligamento no Parque das Águas afetou iluminação e câmeras de segurança.
articles.summary: Decisão prevê multa diária de R$ 30 mil e proíbe novos cortes que atinjam serviços essenciais. Desligamento no Parque das Águas afetou iluminação e câmeras de segurança.
articles.body:
A Justiça Federal determinou, nesta segunda-feira (23), que a Energisa restabeleça em até duas horas o fornecimento de energia elétrica no Parque das Águas, em Cuiabá — Foto: Ianara Garcia/TVCA

A Justiça Federal determinou, nesta segunda-feira (23), que a Energisa restabeleça em até duas horas o fornecimento de energia elétrica no Parque das Águas, em Cuiabá . A decisão foi tomada depois que a concessionária suspendeu a energia de unidades ligadas ao parque . A decisão também abrange o Parque Tia Nair, onde a concessionária também determinou o corte, mas o fornecimento não chegou a ser interrompido.

Ao g1 , a Energisa informou que não havia sido notificada oficialmente até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Se descumprir a ordem, a empresa poderá pagar multa de R$ 30 mil por dia. Segundo a Prefeitura de Cuiabá, o desligamento atingiu duas unidades do Parque das Águas e comprometeu a iluminação e o funcionamento das câmeras de monitoramento do local.

A prefeitura informou à Justiça que os desligamentos ocorreram antes da data prevista em uma notificação enviada pela Energisa à Empresa Cuiabana de Zeladoria e Serviços Urbanos (Limpurb). No documento, a concessionária havia anunciado cortes por falta de pagamento a partir de 30 de novembro.

Para comprovar a suspensão, o município apresentou fotos de funcionários da empresa durante os desligamentos. Ao analisar o pedido, o juiz federal Hiram Armênio Xavier Pereira considerou que a falta de iluminação e a interrupção do monitoramento poderiam comprometer a segurança dos frequentadores.

A Energisa deverá informar à Justiça o horário em que o fornecimento foi restabelecido em cada unidade.

A liminar também suspendeu os desligamentos anunciados para 30 de novembro e proibiu a Energisa de realizar novos cortes por falta de pagamento que atinjam serviços públicos essenciais de Cuiabá.

A decisão segue uma sentença anterior, em uma ação movida pelo Ministério Público Federal (MPF), que protege serviços como iluminação e segurança pública. O juiz também determinou que a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) fiscalize o cumprimento da ordem e apresente, em cinco dias, um relatório sobre as providências adotadas.

Em pronunciamento, o prefeito de Cuiabá afirmou que o corte foi equivocado e disse que o município tem recursos reservados para pagar os valores cobrados pela concessionária, mas contesta as faturas. Segundo ele, a prefeitura aponta que a Energisa deve aproximadamente R$ 73 milhões ao município, enquanto a empresa cobra R$ 9 milhões da prefeitura.

O prefeito afirmou que a divergência envolve, principalmente, a cobrança pelo consumo de energia da iluminação pública após a substituição de mais de 10 mil lâmpadas convencionais por modelos de LED. Segundo ele, as faturas não teriam sido atualizadas para considerar a mudança.

A prefeitura defende que deve pagar pelo consumo efetivo dos equipamentos instalados, e não pelos pontos de iluminação que foram substituídos. O prefeito disse ainda que os valores cobrados pela Energisa estão reservados e que o município pode fazer o pagamento caso haja um acordo sobre as contas.

A concessionária já informou que considera os valores devidos e que entrou na Justiça para cobrar a dívida. A discussão sobre a cobrança continua em uma ação separada na Justiça estadual.

articles.title: Programa Recomeço Mongaguá: bolsa de R$ 1,2 mil para moradores | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa prevê cursos de qualificação e treinamento prático em órgãos municipais, com duração de até 18 meses. Prefeitura tem prazo de 90 dias para regulamentar o programa e definir como será a seleção.
articles.summary: Iniciativa prevê cursos de qualificação e treinamento prático em órgãos municipais, com duração de até 18 meses.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Mongaguá — Foto: Dyego Gonçalves/Prefeitura de Mongaguá

A Prefeitura de Mongaguá , no litoral de São Paulo, sancionou uma lei que cria o Programa Recomeço, iniciativa que oferecerá até 50 vagas para moradores em situação de vulnerabilidade social.

Os participantes receberão uma bolsa mensal de R$ 1,2 mil durante o período de qualificação e treinamento profissional. O valor será atualizado anualmente com base no Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA).

Para concorrer a uma das vagas, é necessário ter 18 anos ou mais, ou ser emancipado, morar em Mongaguá, estar inscrito no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico) e estar fora do mercado de trabalho.

A legislação também estabelece que os candidatos não podem ser aposentados ou pensionistas e devem estar em dia com as obrigações eleitorais e militares.

O Programa Recomeço será dividido em duas etapas: qualificação profissional, por meio de cursos oferecidos pela prefeitura ou por instituições parceiras, e treinamento prático supervisionado em órgãos e entidades da administração municipal.

A participação terá duração inicial de seis meses, com possibilidade de prorrogação até o limite de 18 meses. Segundo a lei, os beneficiários não poderão substituir servidores públicos ou funcionários terceirizados em atividades rotineiras da prefeitura.

O recebimento da bolsa não estabelece vínculo empregatício ou estatutário com o município. Caso o participante consiga um emprego ou comece uma atividade remunerada por conta própria, deverá ser desligado do programa.

A Lei nº 3.531/2026 foi sancionada na quarta-feira (18) e já está em vigor. A partir de agora, a prefeitura tem até 90 dias para publicar o decreto que regulamentará o programa.

O documento deverá estabelecer os critérios de prioridade na seleção, a carga horária mínima, o cronograma e o canal oficial para as inscrições. Como o decreto ainda precisa ser publicado, não há definição sobre o cronograma e o canal de inscrições.

articles.title: An Idaho family settled a medical debt and received $6,000 from the provider, but a collector sued the mother over the cancelled bill later; the state supreme court upheld a finding that the collection suit was frivolous
articles.summary: An Idaho woman was sued by a debt collection company over a medical bill that had already been settled, even after her family received $6,000 from the
articles.body: An Idaho woman was sued by a debt collection company over a medical bill that had already been settled, even after her family received $6,000 from the healthcare provider as part of the agreement. The Idaho Supreme Court has upheld a lower court's finding that the collection lawsuit was frivolous, ruling that the company failed to properly investigate the debt before taking legal action.The case involved Taylor L Wood, whose family had received medical care from physicians employed by Intermountain Emergency Physicians (IEP). The medical debt was assigned to Medical Recovery Services (MRS) for collection.According to the court's November 20 opinion, Wood's family entered into a settlement agreement with IEP and other parties to resolve the dispute. The agreement cancelled the debt, released both sides from claims and required IEP to pay the Woods $6,000.2026-52012-0.pdfHowever, roughly four months later, MRS filed a lawsuit against Wood seeking to recover the same debt.Debt collector sued despite settlement agreementWood responded to the lawsuit by submitting the settlement agreement, arguing that the medical debt had already been resolved. MRS eventually withdrew its complaint, acknowledging that it had been unaware of the agreement between Wood and IEP when it filed the case.The district court subsequently declared Wood the prevailing party and ordered MRS to pay her attorney fees and costs. It found that the company had filed the lawsuit frivolously because it had failed to communicate with IEP and investigate the status of the debt before approaching the court.The company challenged the decision, arguing that the debt had been assigned to it and that it had investigated the claim. However, the Idaho Supreme Court rejected its arguments.Court says collector failed to check whether debt existedThe Supreme Court noted that the settlement had been signed several months before MRS filed its complaint. It also highlighted the company's failure to communicate with IEP and its lawyer's failure to investigate the claim adequately.The court observed that MRS had sent Wood a letter telling her that it would verify the debt if she disputed it in writing. Despite receiving a challenge to the debt, the company proceeded with the lawsuit.The court said MRS had acknowledged that the settlement cancelled the debt and could not maintain a claim to recover money that was no longer owed. It therefore upheld the finding that the lawsuit was frivolous and that Wood was entitled to attorney fees.However, the Supreme Court sent the case back to the district court to reconsider the amount of attorney fees. articles.title: Israel must prepare for another Iran war, ex-Mossad chief says, warns Tehran deal will never hold
articles.summary: Israel is showing little sign of backing down from its threats of another military confrontation with Iran, with former Mossad chief David Barnea now
articles.body: Israel is showing little sign of backing down from its threats of another military confrontation with Iran, with former Mossad chief David Barnea now openly calling for a third war to topple the Islamic Republic's regime.As caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly pushes US President Donald Trump for fresh strikes, Barnea has argued that Israel must seize the right moment to bring down Tehran's leadership, even if it means going to war again.Former Mossad director David Barnea, speaking at the ELNET conference in Jerusalem on Monday, said Israel should be prepared for another war against Iran, arguing that a diplomatic agreement with Tehran would never hold.He said Iran's nuclear ambitions remained fundamentally military in nature and that bringing down the Islamic Republic's regime was the only way to permanently eliminate the threat."We need to act with speed and determination in order to bring about the fall of this regime. If this means going to war again, then that is what we need to do," Barnea said.Asked when Israel should act, he replied, "My answer is at the moment when it is possible." He added that the decision to go to war involved weighing multiple factors and that Israel should strike when circumstances allow.Barnea also warned that a nuclear-armed Iran would threaten countries beyond Israel, saying, "It is today against Israel, tomorrow against Europe."The calls for renewed military action have also exposed divisions within Israel over the urgency of another offensive.Netanyahu has reportedly told senior ministers and security officials that an operation against Iran is "unavoidable" and is pressing Trump to support a fresh campaign.According to Channel 13, an unnamed senior Israeli military officer said Israeli and US central command had already shared and approved operational plans, with the timing now dependent on Trump's decision.However, Netanyahu's position is being challenged by Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and a former IDF chief of staff. Speaking at a party meeting on Monday, Eisenkot said he did not see an immediate Iranian threat that required military action before a new government was formed."I do not currently see a direct and immediate threat to the State of Israel that requires action before a government is formed," he said, according to Channel 12.Eisenkot identified Iran's remaining stockpile of 440 kg of enriched uranium as the country's most serious nuclear threat, arguing that Israel should focus on ensuring it is destroyed or removed.Meanwhile, Trump has shown little appetite for immediately approving another military campaign, despite mounting pressure from Netanyahu.In an interview with Axios on November 19, the US president said he was "not rushing into any decision" on Iran and indicated that he would revisit the possibility of fresh strikes after the beginning of the new year. Trump is weighing whether to give the ongoing naval blockade and economic pressure more time to force Tehran into concessions.However, the military option remains on the table. In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, Trump said he was inclined to order fresh strikes against Iran after the New Year if negotiations failed to produce an agreement.He also issued a warning to Tehran over a possible attempt to breach the US naval blockade, saying, "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy."The difference in approach has left Israel pushing for earlier military action while Washington weighs diplomacy, economic pressure and the risks of another full-scale confrontation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Huang out, Huang back: Why Donald Trump intervened in Nvidia's CEO drama
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly backed Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and said his intervention helped persuade the company's board to reinstate
articles.body: US President Donald Trump publicly backed Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and said his intervention helped persuade the company's board to reinstate the co-founder on Monday. Trump said he spoke to Huang over the weekend and that his administration had assured Nvidia there were "no national security concerns" about his return.The intervention came amid controversy over Huang's admission of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and growing calls from employees, investors and technology leaders for his comeback.“The board decided to do what we wanted them to do,” CNBC quoted Trump as saying after Nvidia announced Huang's reinstatement. He also said he believed his intervention had been important in the board's decision. “Basically, I was represented at the board,” Trump said.Why Trump wanted Huang back at NvidiaTrump's support for Huang was driven, at least publicly, by his belief that the executive's leadership was important for Nvidia and the US economy. The president has a close personal relationship with Huang and had repeatedly backed his return in the days before the board reversed its decision.On Sunday, Trump wrote on Truth Social: “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the company, and also, for the USA.”He reiterated his position on Monday, calling the reinstatement the “correct and proper decision”. In another social media post, Trump said the country “needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.”Trump also said attorney general Todd Blanche had confirmed that the government “does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”Trump appeared to have advance knowledge of the decision. In an interview with PBS News Hour's Liz Landers around 30 minutes before Nvidia announced the reinstatement, he said, “He’s back where he should be, and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong from that standpoint.”'I made the deal'US President Donald Trump said he spoke directly to Nvidia’s board and convinced its members to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after his resignation. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC in a phone interview on Monday. “And I convinced them,” he said, adding, “I made the deal.”Trump said Nvidia’s board had sought assurances over potential national security concerns linked to Huang. The concerns stemmed from his reported relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, and her role at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which was suspected of facilitating the diversion of Nvidia’s advanced chips to China.“And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot,” Trump said. He added that after reaching an understanding with the board, he called Huang and asked him to “work hard”.Trump also said Huang “did nothing wrong” and argued that losing him posed a greater threat to Nvidia than retaining him.How the controversy led to Huang's exitHuang resigned on November 12 after revelations about two extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.The allegations triggered scrutiny of Nvidia, its leadership and its business dealings. Lawmakers and other elected officials sought investigations into Huang's conduct, the company's chip sales and the government's enforcement of export controls.However, US authorities have not reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. Attorney General Blanche told reporters earlier this month that the Justice Department was examining the matter.“All that I think I will say is that of course DOJ is investigating or looking at it," Blanche said.The Justice Department is also conducting a criminal investigation into potential export control violations involving Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm where Alice Huang was an executive. Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations.From rejecting his return to reinstating himNvidia's board had initially resisted bringing Huang back. Chairman Harvey C. Jones told analysts during the company's earnings call last Tuesday that the board had “unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”.Trump's public support, however, grew over the following days. On November 17, he said he “would not mind” seeing Huang reinstated. On Friday, he told reporters at the White House that he “would love to see Jensen be given a second chance”.Huang had also indicated that he was willing to return. On November 17, he said he would be “honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO” if the board believed it was best for the company, its employees, shareholders and the US.The board eventually reversed its position on Monday, reinstating him as president and CEO.“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Jones said in a statement.Huang said he was “honored” to return and would take on the responsibility “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment”. Interim CEO Colette Kress, who led the company during his absence, will return to her role as chief financial officer.Employee petition and tech leaders back HuangTrump's intervention came as support for Huang's return gathered momentum among Nvidia employees and prominent technology executives.An online petition titled “Stand with Jensen”, urging the board to bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, had attracted more than 206,000 signatures by Monday morning, according to its website. More than 10,000 signatories identified themselves as current Nvidia employees.Elon Musk, Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney were among those who signed the petition.“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too,” Musk wrote on X on November 13.The calls for Huang's return came despite criticism from some members of the administration. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent had earlier said Nvidia needed “a dramatic shake-up” and an external CEO. However, in an interview with CBS on Sunday, he said: “I said they should go to the outside, but he's on the outside now”.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: There are few job references more powerful than a recommendation from the President of the United States. Nvidia’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang discovered on Monday that one from Donald Trump can even undo a unanimous boardroom decision.A single social media post by MAGA supremo on Sunday was all it took for the Board of Nvidia to reverse course and reinstate Huang as CEO on a manic Monday morning, sending the company’s stock rocketing up by a staggering 35 per cent within minutes of the announcement and lifting the broader US market.After a transparent intervention by Trump, seemingly in the face of red flags from the US intelligence community, the board said it was satisfied with Huang's candour and ability to lead, and that his return posed no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, who was elevated at the time of Huang’s Nov. 12 ouster to board chairman, said in a statement.It was a remarkable change of heart, particularly after Jones had only recently declared that the board did not intend to bring him back. What happened in between was an extraordinary lobbying campaign, with Trump providing the presidential megaphone on his Truth Social platform and some of the world's most influential tech billionaires, including Elon Musk, supplying the chorus.In a follow-up post after bringing the Board to heel, Trump said “it has made the correct and proper decision” and the US “needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.”“The US Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security. The attorney general has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” the MAGA boss said, adding, "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure."Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and transformed it into the dominant force in AI chips powering the current tech boom, expressed gratitude over his reinstatement. “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” he said, adding, “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment… I can’t wait to get back to work.”Drowned out in the rapture among Huang’s fan club over his return after Trump’s intervention were leaks from the American intelligence community that Alice Huang, the Chinese woman Jensen Huang had an affair with, kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year during her dalliance with the Nvidia boss. US intelligence agencies also gathered evidence that Ms Huang’s business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, according to media reports.All that hardly seemed to matter as America’s tech elite lined up behind Trump to force Huang’s return. Elon Musk, who had even suggested that hiring Huang at one of his own companies would be an honour, while others had urged him to either start a new company or join a rival, declared after the reinstatement, “The mistake has been corrected.” The White House made no secret of Trump’s intervention, calling the Nvidia board’s reversal “a great decision” and echoing Trump’s words that “we have to protect our geniuses.”Indeed, Trump himself had to untangle the conflict within the administration after Huang’s exit appeared to have been forced by China hardliners like Marco Rubio, who reportedly strengthened the language suggesting he was honeytrapped in a Chinese spying operation. But pro-business voices like commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and pro-tech spokespersons like former Trump AI advisor David Sacks questioned the allegations against Huang, arguing that he was being forced out before the facts had been established.Trump, who always seemed to have a sympathetic ear for Huang, went with the latter group. “The US Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” he said in a post on Truth Social, adding, “On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure.”Not everyone was thrilled by the board turnaround after Trump intervention which takes presidential influence in corporate America to a new level as it bows and scrapes before him. Senator Elizabeth Warren was among the critics, calling the reinstatement reckless while demanding that Nvidia's leadership answer questions about export-control compliance. She also asked the Trump administration to disclose which senior officials had advised the board that Huang's return posed no national security risk even as reports continued to filter out about Alice Huang’s ties to Beijing and Jensen Huang’s own intemperate behavior with his associates and subordinates at Nvidia.Indeed, as if the intelligence concerns were not damaging enough, separate disclosures painted a decidedly less flattering portrait of Huang's management style. A New York Times investigation drawing on interviews with more than a dozen current and former employees and two decades of documents and court records, described a corporate culture in which humiliation and intimidation were routinely deployed as management tools at Nvidia.Huang's alleged outbursts were extraordinary even by the standards of Silicon Valley's famously “assoholic bosses.” He reportedly told one executive that his mother should have aborted him, threatened to beat a subordinate with the person's own arms and told another that he would tear off the top of his head and urinate on his brain. In one disturbing account, he reportedly described humiliation as a way of extracting greater performance from employees who had become too wealthy to be motivated by money.The behaviour had generated workplace complaints and, in at least two cases, confidential settlements with former senior executives, according to the NYT. Yet it also described a company where Huang inspired extraordinary devotion, with employees simultaneously revering and fearing him. The devotion expressed itself in an online campaign, dubbed 'Stand with Jensen', which attracted more than 194,000 signatures at its peak, including employees, former employees, shareholders and technology industry figures.You use AI every day. articles.title: Do you have one of these 20 British surnames? More than 5,500 unclaimed estates await rightful heirs across England and Wales, with a fortune potentially waiting to be claimed
articles.summary: Imagine discovering that a distant relative you never knew existed has left behind an estate that could legally belong to you.
articles.body: Imagine discovering that a distant relative you never knew existed has left behind an estate that could legally belong to you. It may sound like the plot of a film, but thousands of families across England and Wales could have a similar story waiting to unfold.The UK Government has revealed that more than 5,500 estates remain unclaimed after people died without leaving a valid will or an identifiable heir. Among them are people whose relatives may still be entitled to inherit their money and property. And if your family name appears on the list of frequently occurring surnames, it could be worth investigating your family history.According to information reported by The Mirror, Wales Online and Daily Express, the Government's Bona Vacantia Division (BVD) maintains a public register of unclaimed estates. It includes details of people who died without a valid will and whose estates have been referred to the authorities because no rightful beneficiary has come forward.The register features thousands of names, but some surnames appear far more frequently than others. Here are 20 of the most common surnames found among the unclaimed estates.20 British surnames appearing most frequently on the unclaimed estates listSurnameNumber of estatesSmith94Jones53Brown45Williams39Taylor29Davies28Wilson26Johnson25Thomas23Harris22Kelly21Martin20Ryan20White19James18King18Davis17Edwards17Evans16Clark16Smith tops the list with 94 unclaimed estates, followed by Jones with 53 and Brown with 45. Williams and Taylor complete the top five, with 39 and 29 estates respectively.However, having one of these surnames does not automatically mean you are entitled to an inheritance. The list is only a starting point for people trying to establish whether they have a family connection to someone who died without a will.Who gets the money when someone dies without leaving a will?When a person dies without a valid or effective will, they are legally described as having died intestate. In such cases, inheritance is decided according to the rules of intestacy rather than personal wishes or informal family arrangements.The surviving husband, wife or civil partner generally has the first claim, followed by children, grandchildren and other direct descendants. If there are no eligible descendants, the estate may pass to parents, siblings and their children, grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins, according to the legal order of entitlement.The rules also distinguish between full and half-blood relatives. For instance, half-brothers and half-sisters share only one parent with the deceased, while half-uncles and half-aunts share one grandparent rather than both.How long do relatives have to claim an unclaimed estate?The Government's Bona Vacantia Division gives potential heirs a limited period to establish their claim. For estates involving money, the general deadline is 12 years from the date the estate was referred to the Crown. In certain circumstances, interest may be payable for claims made within this period.Other assets, such as property, may remain claimable for up to 30 years after death.Anyone who believes they could be related to a person on the register must provide evidence of their connection. This usually involves preparing a family tree supported by birth, marriage and death certificates and other relevant records.How can you check whether a relative has left behind an unclaimed estate?The Government regularly updates its Bona Vacantia list with details of unclaimed estates in England and Wales. The register generally includes the deceased person's name, date of death and place of death.Potential heirs can search the official Government register to see whether they recognise a name or identify a possible family connection. If they find a match, they must establish their relationship through documentary evidence before making a claim.Importantly, the process is not based on surnames alone. Thousands of people can share the same family name without having any connection to one another.If no rightful heir comes forward, the estate may eventually pass to the Crown. Scotland and Northern Ireland operate separate systems for administering unclaimed estates, so the England and Wales register does not cover the entire UK.For anyone interested in tracing their family history, the list could offer an unexpected starting point. A familiar surname may catch your attention, but it is the family connection and supporting documents that ultimately determine whether an inheritance can be claimed.You use AI every day. articles.title: A British Columbia father cut his daughter out of his will, believing she had chosen to estrange herself for 10 years; they later reconciled, and a judge has now awarded her 45% of his $1.8 million estate
articles.summary: A British Columbia father who cut his daughter out of his will, believing she had chosen to estrange herself from him for around 10 years, has been
articles.body: A British Columbia father who cut his daughter out of his will, believing she had chosen to estrange herself from him for around 10 years, has been ordered to leave her 45% of his estate worth nearly $1.9 million. Daniel Alan Dancey had left the entire residue of his estate to his son in his 2022 will, making no provision for his daughter, Kristin Danielle Enes. However, the pair reconciled months before his death in January 2024. Now, a judge has ruled that his reasons for disinheriting her were not defensible and ordered the estate to be divided between his two children.Why did a judge give a disinherited daughter 45% of her father's estateAccording to the judgment in Enes v. Dancey, Daniel Alan Dancey died on January 12, 2024, leaving an estate valued at more than $1.8 million. His final will, signed on September 29, 2022, made specific provisions for his former wife, Cindy, and his three grandchildren, but excluded his daughter entirely.The will left $10,000 to Cindy, $1,000 to each of his three grandchildren and the entire residue of the estate to his son, Jeffery, who was also named as executor. The judge noted that Dan had disinherited Kristin because he believed she had chosen to estrange herself from him for approximately 10 years. Kristin challenged the distribution under British Columbia's Wills, Estates and Succession Act, arguing that her father had no valid and rational reason to leave her out of his will.Why did Dan and Kristin's relationship break downKristin and her brother grew up in Coquitlam, where their father operated an HVAC business. The family had previously shared a close relationship, with regular Sunday dinners, birthday celebrations and holiday gatherings. However, their family circumstances changed after Dan and Cindy separated in 2011. Kristin invited her mother to live with her after the separation, which contributed to tension between Kristin and her father. Their relationship improved for a period in 2012 but deteriorated again in 2014, following Kristin's separation and eventual divorce from her husband, Noah Enes.The judgment also referred to a public Facebook post Dan made in September 2014, in which he wrote: "funny how life is rolling along when your daughter dumps her husband and kids. Disappointment not really." The court heard that Dan blamed Kristin for the breakdown of her marriage and subsequently reduced her inheritance in earlier versions of his will. A 2015 will indicated an intention to reduce her share to 1%, while a March 2020 will allocated her 1% of the estate and gave the remaining shares to other beneficiaries. In September 2022, Dan also prepared a letter stating that he had been cut out of his daughter's life for 10 years and requesting that she receive nothing from his estate.How did Dan and Kristin reconcile before his deathThe relationship began to change in June 2023, when Kristin and Dan attended the funeral of Kristin's uncle, Tony. The judgment recorded that Kristin approached her father to ask about his health, which led to a conversation and, eventually, an embrace. They also made plans to get together to celebrate Dan's grandson's birthday. Following the funeral, they began exchanging text messages regularly, arranged family gatherings and attended a car show together with other family members.Justice Hoffman rejected the argument that the reconciliation was not genuine. The judge found that the messages between them showed they regularly communicated, supported one another emotionally, shared jokes and discussed common interests. Dan had also discussed his frustration with Jeffery and his thoughts about changing his will again. The judgment stated: "By 2023, Dan was reconciled with Kristin such that he was sharing with her his frustrations with Jeffery, as well as his thoughts about once again altering his will."The court also considered the reasons behind the earlier estrangement and whether Kristin was responsible for the breakdown in their relationship. Justice Hoffman concluded that the estrangement had originated with Dan's disappointment over Kristin's divorce and that Kristin had made attempts to repair their relationship. The judge stated that "Dan’s disappointment that Kristin divorced Noah is not a valid and rationale reason to disinherit her." The court further found that, by the time of Dan's death, the earlier letter explaining his decision to exclude Kristin no longer accurately reflected his views about her.Why did the judge consider Kristin's financial situationIn assessing the inheritance dispute, the court considered several factors, including the size of the estate, Kristin's financial circumstances, the contributions made by both children and Jeffery's competing claim. Kristin was a single mother raising three children and had two mortgages totalling $275,000 on her home. She had generally worked part-time to remain available for her children and had experienced job losses in recent years. The judge found that her financial circumstances weighed in favour of varying the will.The court also acknowledged that Jeffery had made greater contributions to his father's care during the final years of his life. He had lived in the family home since April 2019, driven Dan to medical appointments, run errands and brought him food. However, the judge found that these contributions were not sufficient to remove Dan's moral obligation to provide for Kristin. The judgment also noted that Jeffery's financial difficulties were, to a significant extent, connected to his personal choices regarding employment.Why did the judge award Kristin 45% of her father's estateIn the final ruling, Justice Hoffman concluded that Dan had not made adequate provision for Kristin and had not acted as a judicious testator because his reasons for disinheriting her were not defensible. The judge determined that Jeffery's moral claim was slightly stronger because of the care he had provided to their father, but that this did not justify leaving Kristin without an inheritance.The court therefore ordered that the 2022 will be varied so that the residue of Dan's estate would be divided, with 45% going to Kristin and 55% to Jeffery. It also ordered an accounting of Dan's assets before and after his death, with the assets or their value to be transferred into his estate. The judge further ruled that Jeffery, both as executor and in his personal capacity, held his interest in the estate property in trust for Kristin.Disclaimer: This article is based on information publicly available. The Times of India has not independently verified the details of the family dispute, the estate's value or the court's findings mentioned. The information should not be interpreted as confirmation from Kristin Danielle Enes, Jeffery Dancey, the estate of Daniel Alan Dancey or their representatives.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2010, a Nebraska couple financed $100,000 of a building sale; after the buyer stopped paying in 2012, the state Supreme Court upheld foreclosure in 2026 on a lien that grew to $247,068
articles.summary: A building sale that began with a $100,000 seller-financed loan turned into a lengthy foreclosure dispute after the buyer stopped making payments.
articles.body: A building sale that began with a $100,000 seller-financed loan turned into a lengthy foreclosure dispute after the buyer stopped making payments. More than a decade later, the unpaid obligation had grown to over $247,000, prompting a legal challenge over whether the sellers had waited too long to enforce their rights against the property.In an opinion issued on November 20, 2026, available on Justia, the Nebraska Supreme Court upheld a foreclosure judgment in favour of Alex and Janice Hinrichsen against RCTS Properties, L.L.C. The court concluded that neither the bankruptcy filing of a company member nor the sellers' submission of a bankruptcy claim had triggered the deadline for foreclosure. It also rejected the buyer's argument that older unpaid instalments should be excluded from the amount secured by the property.A $100,000 loan remained unpaid after 2012The dispute originated in December 2010, when RCTS Properties purchased a building in Elm Creek, Nebraska, from the Hinrichsens. The buyer paid part of the purchase price upfront, while the couple financed the remaining $100,000.On December 31, 2010, the company signed a promissory note agreeing to repay the amount in monthly instalments beginning in March 2011, with the final payment scheduled for January 2026. The loan was secured by a deed of trust on the property. The company's members, Chad Messersmith and Jeffrey Moore, signed the note on its behalf, while Messersmith also personally guaranteed the debt.RCTS made payments for just over a year but stopped after its May 2012 instalment. In August that year, Messersmith filed for personal bankruptcy. The following month, the Hinrichsens submitted a proof of claim seeking $121,624.96, covering his liability under the guarantee and another obligation. Messersmith's personal liability under the guarantee was subsequently discharged in bankruptcy, and the Hinrichsens received no payment.Why the buyer challenged the foreclosureThe dispute resurfaced in October 2022, when RCTS demanded that the deed of trust be reconveyed, arguing that the loan was no longer enforceable because the limitation period had expired. The Hinrichsens refused. In December 2023, they demanded $222,952.87, including more than a decade of default interest. Their lawyers stated that they had the authority to accelerate the loan and begin foreclosure if the default was not corrected.The couple filed a judicial foreclosure action in February 2024. RCTS argued that the 10-year limitation period for foreclosure had started in 2012, either when Messersmith filed for bankruptcy or when the Hinrichsens submitted their proof of claim. If that period had begun then, the company argued, the 2024 foreclosure action was too late.However, the Nebraska Supreme Court found that neither event amounted to an effective acceleration of the debt. Under state law, when acceleration is optional, a creditor must take clear and unequivocal action showing an intention to demand immediate repayment of the entire outstanding balance.The court explained that filing a bankruptcy claim establishes a creditor's right to payment but does not necessarily demand immediate payment of the full debt. It also noted that Messersmith's bankruptcy filing was not an action taken by the Hinrichsens to accelerate the loan.Court upholds the $247,068 foreclosure amountRCTS raised another objection, arguing that a five-year limitation period applicable to written contract claims should prevent the sellers from including instalments that had become due more than five years before the foreclosure lawsuit. The Nebraska Supreme Court rejected this argument, distinguishing between an action to recover money under a written contract and an action to foreclose on property securing a debt.It explained that Nebraska law provides a 10-year limitation period for judicial foreclosure actions. This period applies even when a separate action to recover the debt under the promissory note may be time-barred. The court rejected RCTS's argument that the five-year limitation period for written contract claims should exclude older missed instalments. It also noted that RCTS had not challenged the inclusion of instalments due more than 10 years before the foreclosure action. The district court had determined that the Hinrichsens were entitled to foreclosure for $247,068.43.Under the foreclosure decree, RCTS was given 20 days to pay the amount due. If it failed to do so, the property could be sold and the proceeds applied towards the outstanding obligation. The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed the lower court's decision, leaving the foreclosure judgment intact.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A British couple in their 70s fought eviction from a housing association flat over electricity charges; after winning their appeal, a High Court judge allowed £1,488 they had borrowed for AI-assisted legal research
articles.summary: A British couple in their 70s who represented themselves in a fight to save their home have won the right to recover £1,488 spent on an artificial
articles.body: A British couple in their 70s who represented themselves in a fight to save their home have won the right to recover £1,488 spent on an artificial intelligence (AI) legal research tool. The High Court allowed the expense, finding that the subscription had been purchased specifically to help them prepare their case. The judgment was delivered on November 19.Linda Foster and Richard Hitchens had challenged eviction proceedings brought by Wargrave on Thames Housing Association over a dispute involving electricity charges. Unable to afford legal advice or obtain legal aid, they handled the case themselves. They borrowed money from Hitchens's brother to pay for the AI subscription.Dispute over electricity chargesThe dispute began when the housing association sought to recover electricity costs from the couple. Their tenancy agreement listed electricity charges separately from rent, service charges and water charges.The association argued that the electricity payment covered both heating inside their flat and electricity used for communal facilities. Foster and Hitchens disagreed. They maintained that the charge applied only to electricity supplied for underfloor or background heating in their home.The couple had stopped paying the disputed amount. They also avoided using the underfloor heating because they considered it unsafe. The housing association treated the unpaid charges as a breach of the tenancy agreement and sought possession of their flat.The High Court later found that the electricity charge was limited to heating supplied to the couple's premises. Costs relating to communal facilities could not be recovered under that particular provision. The possession order was therefore set aside.Court allows £1,488 AI subscription costAfter winning the appeal, the couple sought reimbursement of the expenses incurred while representing themselves. Their claim included £1,488 for an AI-powered legal research subscription. They had paid £124 a month for 12 months.They told the court that the tool helped them find relevant legal decisions, research the dispute and prepare submissions. They had selected a specialised legal research service rather than a general-purpose or free AI chatbot.The housing association opposed the claim, arguing that the subscription was an overhead rather than a recoverable legal expense.Mr Justice Sweeting agreed that the subscription did not amount to a legal service because the provider had supplied software, not legal advice or representation. However, he said this did not prevent the expense from being considered separately as a litigation disbursement.The judge examined how the couple had used the service and why they had purchased it. He noted that they were pensioners living in social housing and could neither obtain legal aid nor afford professional advice.He also found that their written and oral submissions were focused and carefully prepared, helping them succeed on the main issue in the appeal. The subscription had been purchased specifically for the proceedings and was not maintained for other purposes. The judge therefore allowed the full £1,488.He made clear that this did not mean AI subscription costs would automatically be recoverable in other cases. Courts would have to consider the purpose of the expense, the nature of the service and whether the amount was reasonable and proportionate. He also cautioned that using AI to generate lengthy and unhelpful material could lead to costs being rejected.Judge reduces couple's wider costs claimThe couple had also claimed payment for 649 hours spent on research, preparing documents, correspondence and attending hearings.However, the judge considered this excessive for a dispute centred on the interpretation of the tenancy agreement. He reduced the amount allowed for their time to £5,600, around 40% of the sum claimed.The court separately allowed £1,246 for expenses such as court fees, transcripts and travel. It also approved £888 for their work on proceedings following the appeal, along with £220 in expenses.The judge refused to order the housing association to refund electricity charges the couple had already paid. He said the appeal had established that the disputed amounts could not all be recovered under the particular electricity charge provision, but had not established that every previous payment was refundable.You use AI every day. articles.title: Rail passenger traffic to cross pre-Covid level, touch 820 crore this fiscal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Railway passenger traffic is expected to touch pre-Covid levels of around 800 crore by March 2027, while freight movement is also projected to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Railway passenger traffic is expected to touch pre-Covid levels of around 800 crore by March 2027, while freight movement is also projected to reach an all-time high, a top ministry official said on Monday.In 2019-20, railways carried 808.6 crore passengers and going by the projection, this year it’s likely to be around 820 crore. “There is a lot of focus on increasing the number of trains and facilities for passengers. We have introduced around 2,500 new passenger trains over the past five years to meet growing demand and expand connectivity,” the official said.Highlighting the expansion of services during the festive season, railway ministry officials said around 18,000 additional trains were operated during Durga Puja, Diwali and Chhath this year. These services transported nearly 20 crore additional passengers, around 8% more than in the corresponding festive period last year.Officials also highlighted the railways efforts to increase its share in the country’s freight transportation market by diversifying its cargo basket and introducing measures to attract more commodities to the railway network. “The share of goods transported by rail has increased from around 27% earlier to nearly 30% now,” an official said, adding that the focus has been on expanding the range of commodities carried by the national transporter and improving logistics efficiency.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US flight disruptions: Chicago's O'Hare airport issues brief ground stop over staffing shortage
articles.summary: A ground stop was issued at US' Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport on Monday morning due to staffing constraints, briefly disrupting flight operations
articles.body: A ground stop was issued at US' Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport on Monday morning due to staffing constraints, briefly disrupting flight operations as millions of Americans prepare to travel for Thanksgiving.The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered departures to O’Hare to remain grounded at 10:40 am (local time). The stoppage expired at 12:15 pm (local time).“The FAA is briefly pausing flights into Chicago O’Hare International Airport due to staffing constraints at Chicago Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON),” the agency told Fox Chicago in a statement.Around a dozen flights were cancelled at O’Hare over the past 24 hours, while delays averaged about 15 minutes.The disruption comes just a day after a technical glitch at Delta Air Lines delayed more than 1,000 flights across the US. The airline’s automated system for calculating aircraft weight and balance malfunctioned on Sunday, forcing staff to use manual procedures. The FAA briefly halted Delta flights bound for Atlanta, the airline’s main hub, at its request. Delta later said the system had been restored.The latest disruption comes amid a busy Thanksgiving travel period. AAA estimates that nearly 6 million people will take domestic flights during the holiday, up around 7 per cent from last year.The incidents follow a nationwide FAA ground stop on November 13, when a telecommunications failure disrupted air traffic control systems across the US. The FAA halted flights across the country for more than four hours before lifting the order at around 8:15 pm ET. The disruption led to thousands of cancellations, with the FAA later reporting that around 12,462 flights were cancelled that day.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: An Amtrak train carrying 95 passengers partially derailed after colliding with a semitruck in the US state of Louisiana, injuring five people, authorities said.The crash occurred on Sunday evening when the train struck an 18-wheeler carrying a bulldozer at a railroad crossing east of Lafayette, according to the Lafayette Fire Department.Photos of the scene showed a derailed train car sitting upright in a field, facing away from the tracks. The bulldozer was lying on its side beside the railway, with parts of it torn apart.Sgt Ashley Wood of the Lafayette Police Department said the truck was crossing the railroad tracks when the collision occurred, as reported by AP.Firefighters helped passengers evacuate the train once it was safe to do so. The five people injured sustained minor injuries, Lafayette Mayor-President Monique Blanco Boulet said in a social media post.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
