articles.title: Indian-origin billionaire Neil Mehta, wife Jash announce $6 million donation to Trump Accounts for San Francisco children
articles.summary: Billionaire venture capitalist Neil Mehta and his wife, Jash, announced their contribution of around $6 million to fund $100 to each of the 60,000
articles.body: Billionaire venture capitalist Neil Mehta and his wife, Jash, announced their contribution of around $6 million to fund $100 to each of the 60,000 children in San Francisco through Trump Accounts. The initiative will give every eligible child born between 2016 and 2024 in the city $100 through the Trump Accounts programme, which allows money to be invested in the stock market and grow over time.“San Francisco has always been a place that believes tomorrow can be better than today,” Neil Mehta said. “It’s why this city has produced so many extraordinary inventions and opportunities. Jash and I want the kids growing up here to feel that same sense of optimism and to own a small piece of the future that it creates.”"The future is going to be wile and wonderful. Own a piece of it," the donor message from the Mehtas read in Trump Accounts.Michae Dell thanked Jash and Neil and called the donation "amazing and wonderful". Michael Dell and Susan Dell committed $6.25 billion to deposit $250 each into the 530A Trump Accounts of 25 million US children.Parents will have to claim and activate their children's accounts through the official government app to receive the contributiosn. The money will remain invested until January 1 of the year the child turns 18. After that, the accounts will be governed by rules similar to those applicable to traditional individual retirement accounts (IRAs), meaning withdrawals could attract taxes or penalties.Children born between 2025 and 2028 are separately eligible for $1,000 in federal seed money under the programme, provided they meet the citizenship and Social Security number requirements. The Mehtas' contribution extends the benefit to an older group of children who do not qualify for that federal seed funding.Who are Neil Mehta and Jash?Neil Mehta is the founder and managing partner of Greenoaks Capital, a prominent investment firm that he co-founded in 2012. He grew up in San Francisco and previously worked at hedge fund DE Shaw before establishing Greenoaks. The investment firm has backed several major technology companies, including Korean e-commerce giant Coupang, cybersecurity company Wiz, artificial intelligence companies Anthropic and Databricks, and financial technology company Stripe. Mehta remained on Coupang's board through its 2021 public listing.Mehta has also become a prominent investor in San Francisco's real estate and community revitalisation efforts. In 2024, he committed $100 million to an initiative aimed at reviving historic buildings and commercial properties along the city's Fillmore Street. He said he had donated his financial interest in the project to a nonprofit. However, the acquisitions attracted criticism from community groups concerned about the displacement of local businesses and the influence of wealthy investors.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt has warned that leaving WhatsApp Web logged in on a shared computer can expose users' accounts to unauthorised access.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt has warned that leaving WhatsApp Web logged in on a shared computer can expose users' accounts to unauthorised access. In an advisory, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the ministry of home affairs, urged users to log out manually after every session, particularly on office computers and other devices that people can access.The advisory, issued by I4C's National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, said someone who gains access to an active session could read private messages, view contacts and group chats, and send messages while posing as the account holder. That could give fraudsters a way to approach friends, relatives or colleagues from an account they already recognise and trust.The queries sent to Meta, which owns WhatsApp, remained unanswered.I4C said a WhatsApp Web session can remain active after the browser tab or window is closed. It advised users to avoid signing in from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres or borrowed computers. For temporary use on a trusted computer, it recommended opening a private window and manually logging out before closing it.The advisory also urged users to avoid exchanging confidential information through WhatsApp Web. It asked them to take unexplained account activity seriously, including messages they did not send or unexpected replies from contacts. Users were also advised to keep their operating systems, browsers and security software updated and avoid suspicious downloads and untrusted applications.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: SC grants bail to Godhra train burning convict on medical grounds
articles.summary: New Delhi: Supreme Court Monday granted bail on medical grounds to Irfan Siraj Pada, one of the convicts in the Godhra train burning case.
articles.body: New Delhi: Supreme Court Monday granted bail on medical grounds to Irfan Siraj Pada, one of the convicts in the Godhra train burning case.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale suspended the sentence as Pada is suffering from serious cardiovascular disease and the state accepted his medical condition. He has been in jail for around 18 years."Counsel for state submits that condition of the petitioner as submitted by the senior counsel appearing for the petitioner is factually correct. In view of the aforementioned factual scenario, we are inclined to grant suspension of sentence to the petitioner on medical grounds," the bench said.The train burning took place on Feb 27, 2002, killing 58 people inside the S6 coach of Sabarmati Express. In March 2011, the trial court had convicted 31 people, of whom 11 were sentenced to death and the remaining 20 were awarded life in prison. Sixty-three other accused were acquitted. In 2017, Gujarat HC commuted the death sentence of the 11 convicts to life terms and upheld the life sentences awarded to the other 20. The appeals filed by the convicts in SC have been pending since 2018. TNNGet the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bisleri controversy puts industry in hot water
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Even as Bisleri on Monday said its mineral water is \"safe for consumption, following stringent 90-odd quality checks\", the FSSAI action against
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Even as Bisleri on Monday said its mineral water is "safe for consumption, following stringent 90-odd quality checks", the FSSAI action against the popular brand has put the spotlight on compliance and raised the bar across the nearly $4 billion packaged water industry.With Bisleri International accounting for an estimated 60% of the packaged water market, the action may have wider implications across the sector on quality controls, manufacturing processes and labelling practices, industry experts told TOI.The development comes after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) Sunday initiated prosecution against the country's most widely recognised packaged water brand after a sample was found non-compliant with prescribed safety standards.On Monday, the scrutiny seems to have extended beyond Bisleri, with testing and investigations covering other players in the industry. The market led by players such as Bisleri, Coca-Cola's Kinley, PepsiCo's Aquafina and Tata Consumer Products' Himalayan, continues to project a positive long-term growth trajectory, underpinned by population growth, rising per-capita consumption and increasing penetration of branded packaged water across consumer segments.Bisleri could face a short-term impact, but the larger outcome should be a more accountable industry and better consumer protection, notes Lloyd Mathias, independent director, who had stints in senior leadership roles in FMCG and telecom companies. "The tightening of compliance norms is a long overdue move and will ultimately benefit consumers. The packaged water industry has operated with considerable flexibility (on standards), with definitions around purity, mineral content and even the addition of minerals or vitamins often remaining fluid. These need to be clearly and strictly defined, as they are in developed markets, with transparent labelling so consumers know exactly what they are drinking. Companies have also been relatively casual about the labelling (on the pack)," he said.Further, the compliance on the sector has increased over the last two years since it moved under the ambit of FSSAI as a "high-risk food" category in Nov 2024, following the removal of BIS.Typically, enforcement and monitoring in the industry has been weak, allowing even substandard and fake brands to operate. "Greater regulatory oversight is a positive step towards ensuring consistent quality and consumer safety," said an industry expert. Many see it similar to 2003, when CSE's findings on pesticide residue in soft drinks, triggered a wider review of food safety standards and testing.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Taylor Swift’s Vienna concerts were saved from an ISIS-inspired terror plot by Israel’s Mossad, former chief David Barnea reveals; attack could have killed hundreds
articles.summary: Taylor Swift’s three concerts in Vienna were cancelled in August 2024 after authorities uncovered an ISIS-inspired terror plot.
articles.body: Taylor Swift’s three concerts in Vienna were cancelled in August 2024 after authorities uncovered an ISIS-inspired terror plot. At the time, the decision left thousands of fans heartbroken and raised serious questions about the threat that had forced the singer to call off her performances. Now, a former Israeli intelligence chief has revealed how Mossad helped Austrian authorities prevent what he described as a potential mass-casualty attack.David Barnea, who was then heading Israel’s Mossad, disclosed that the agency played a key role in identifying the network behind the planned attack. Speaking at the European Leadership Network (ELNET) conference in Jerusalem on Monday, he said the operation was made possible through intelligence-sharing between Austria and Israel.According to Barnea, the threat was first identified by Austrian intelligence before the information was passed on to Mossad.How Mossad helped uncover the Vienna concert plot“The initial threat warning came from our Austrian partners,” Barnea said, according to the transcript of his speech.He explained that once the information reached Mossad, Israeli intelligence used its capabilities to analyse the threat, uncover the network and help Austrian authorities move towards the suspects’ arrests.“The moment this information was shared with the Mossad, we successfully [used] our unique capabilities in processing intelligence, cracking infrastructure, leading to the arrest of the global jihadist cell,” he said.Barnea described the joint operation as one that prevented “mass murder”, potentially saving the lives of hundreds of young Europeans.His remarks offer a fresh account of the international intelligence effort behind the foiled attack. Previous reports had highlighted the role of American intelligence, with the Biden administration confirming in August 2024 that the US had shared information with Austrian authorities.Three Taylor Swift concerts were cancelled at the last minuteThe threat came just a day before Swift was due to take the stage at Vienna’s Ernst Happel Stadium. Austrian authorities arrested the principal suspect, who was 19 at the time, on August 7, 2024.The discovery forced organisers to cancel all three of the singer’s sold-out Vienna shows, which were part of her record-breaking Eras Tour. More than 170,000 people were expected to attend the concerts, according to estimates by Austrian news agency APA.Investigators said the suspect had pledged allegiance to the Islamic State (ISIS) and was preparing a suicide attack intended to cause mass casualties. Authorities reportedly found chemicals, machetes and electronic devices at his home.According to investigators, the suspected plan involved targeting crowds outside the stadium. Thousands of fans without tickets were also expected to gather in the area, making the threat particularly serious.For fans who had travelled to see Swift, the cancellations were devastating. The singer later addressed the incident on social media, acknowledging the disappointment while expressing gratitude to the authorities who had prevented a possible tragedy.“Thanks to them, we were grieving concerts and not lives,” she wrote in August 2024.Suspects later received prison sentencesThe investigation continued long after the concerts were cancelled. In May, an Austrian court sentenced two men for their roles in the plot.A 21-year-old identified as Beran A. received a 15-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to terror offences and other charges. Another 21-year-old, identified as Arda K., was sentenced to 12 years.During the proceedings, Beran A. reportedly described receiving instructions and attempting, unsuccessfully, to make a bomb. He had also sought advice on weapons through several chat groups and from a senior ISIS member.In a separate development, a Berlin court last year convicted a 16-year-old Syrian teenager of contributing to the plot. He received an 18-month suspended sentence.Barnea also spoke about other alleged terror networks in EuropeThe former Mossad chief’s remarks at the Jerusalem conference went beyond the Taylor Swift concert plot. He also discussed Israeli intelligence cooperation with European agencies over alleged Iranian-directed assassination attempts and Hamas networks accused of planning attacks against Jewish and Israeli targets.Barnea claimed that joint intelligence work helped expose an alleged Iranian network in Greece and North Macedonia, as well as cells in France and Germany. He also spoke about investigations with German, Austrian and Danish authorities that allegedly uncovered Hamas infrastructure and hidden weapons stockpiles in Vienna, Bulgaria and Poland.These were separate investigations from the ISIS-inspired plot targeting Taylor Swift’s Vienna concerts.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Terrible governor': Trump targets Newsom in DOJ speech over decision to commute 548 death sentences
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday launched a sharp attack on California Governor Gavin Newsom over his decision to commute the death sentences of 548
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday launched a sharp attack on California Governor Gavin Newsom over his decision to commute the death sentences of 548 prisoners.In a speech at the Justice Department, Trump called Newsom a “terrible” governor, added that the decision had betrayed the families of murder victims whose relatives were killed by the prisoners.“We come together to stand against the travesty and to wrap our arms around the families of victims who were so brutally betrayed by bad government and our political system,” Trump said at the event, which was attended by families of murder victims, as quoted by Reuters.Trump was joined by Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel. Blanche said the Justice Department was pursuing capital punishment in cases where it was warranted, adding that the department had sought the death penalty 49 times since the start of the administration.“Mr. President, I assure you that this Department of Justice is seeking the death penalty whenever appropriate for crimes committed in this country,” Blanche said while introducing Trump.Newsom's office defended the decision, saying in a post on X that every prisoner whose sentence had been commuted would still die behind bars. The governor had announced plans earlier this month to commute all 548 death sentences in California to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. Many of the commutations require approval from the California Supreme Court.In a video released before Trump's remarks, Newsom accused the president of corruption, saying he was selling pardons and using the Justice Department as his “personal law firm”.Newsom has defended his position against capital punishment, arguing that it is morally wrong and inconsistent with California's values. The state has not carried out an execution since 2006, although voters rejected ballot measures to abolish the death penalty in 2012 and 2016.The governor's decision has drawn criticism from prosecutors and some victims' families. Supporters of the move argue that capital punishment is expensive, inconsistently applied and carries the risk of wrongful convictions.The issue also gives Trump an opportunity to revive his political attack that Democrats are weak on crime, as Newsom weighs a possible run for the presidency in 2028. At Monday's event, relatives of murder victims joined Trump on stage to condemn the commutations and praise his tough-on-crime approach.The president's appearance at the department was unusual, as presidents have traditionally avoided using the Justice Department's platform to directly attack political opponents, given the agency's longstanding expectation of independence from the White House.The visit also comes amid scrutiny of the Trump administration's use of federal law enforcement against political rivals and other perceived adversaries. Since Trump's return to office, the Justice Department has pursued investigations involving several of his critics, although some cases have faced setbacks in courts and grand juries.Trump last addressed the Justice Department in March last year, when he used a speech on crime and immigration to revisit his own criminal prosecutions and accuse officials who had investigated him of misconduct.You use AI every day. articles.title: China’s mega dam takes shape near Arunachal Pradesh: Satellite data
articles.summary: Satellite analysis shows China’s 60GW Medog dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo nearing the Arunachal border, with village clearances and diversion works since 2025.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Fresh satellite imagery analysis by an Indian geospatial AI deep tech start-up incubated at FITT, IIT Delhi, shows construction of China’s 60 GW Medog hydropower project on Yarlung Tsangpo (the Siang in India) is advanced and widespread.According to the findings of the public-release assessment by EarthSense Labs, entire villages had been cleared at the main dam site, river diversion works were visible and heavy industrial infrastructure had been built near the Arunachal Pradesh border.The findings are significant for India as it has proposed the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh. Project proponents say SUMP is intended to cushion the downstream impact of the Chinese project.The Chinese project is close to the McMahon Line, about 40 km to 50 km north of Arunachal Pradesh.The EarthSense report places the tunnel exit near the border, downstream of Medog County. The SUMP, proposed on Siang river, would be located further downstream in India, across Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts. Its proposed reservoir is expected by project proponents to hold nine billion cubic metres of water.The Chinese project will be a multi-structure dam system along the lower Yarlung Tsangpo river in southeastern Tibet. It will include a tunnel across the river’s famous “Great U-Bend”, multiple power stations and outlets before the river enters India, the report said.The report lists four critical locations and assets — a large dam near Mainling town, where “work has started extensively after July 2025”; a lower dam, possibly near Pai town; a tunnel through Namcha Barwa Mountain; and a tunnel outlet near the India-China border, downstream of Medog County, where work has also started.“Developmental work on the tunnel outlet area has started even before the ground-breaking ceremony,” the report said.The project is planned as five cascade stations at an estimated cost of 1.2 trillion yuan (roughly $168 billion). It would use tunnels of around 40 km to exploit a river drop of more than 2,000 metres over a stretch of about 50 km, the report said.EarthSense Labs’ study of imagery from July 2025 showed villages and farm fields at the site of the proposed Mainling high dam. By Dec 2025, the villages were cleared, the fields removed and earthwork had begun, it said.Imagery of Aug 2026 showed diversion works, the relocation of entire villages and the emergence of new roads, makeshift housing and office buildings on the north bank.The key finding, according to the report, was “Site clearance and earthwork after July 2025, followed by river diversion works by Aug 2026.”Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu has pointed out that the proposed SUMP reservoir, with a storage capacity of about 9.2 billion cubic metres (BCM), is expected to give India greater control over downstream flows. Khandu had said the Siang reservoir, with a capacity greater than the reported 5.2 BCM of China’s project, would help regulate river flows, respond to sudden changes in upstream discharge and maintain water availability during lean seasons. Khandu has repeatedly flagged the absence of a binding water-sharing treaty and transparent data-sharing arrangement with China as a major vulnerability.Opposition to SUMP has hardened on the ground. Adi communities have petitioned Union home minister Amit Shah, citing concerns over displacement, land and livelihoods. Central armed police forces were deployed near the proposed site as tensions rose over a pre-feasibility survey. In Oct, violence broke out during protests.The report documents the scale and pace of construction but does not quantify environmental damage, downstream flow effects or risks to Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. Its locations are described as indicative, and the analysis relies on satellite imagery.KEY FINDINGSMainling high dam· July 2025: Imagery shows villages and farm fields.December 2025: Villages cleared, fields removed and earthwork begun.August 2026: Diversion works visible and entire villages relocated. New roads, makeshift housing and office buildings have appeared on the north bank.Pai Town low dam siteNo conclusive structural work found as of October 2026.EarthSense says “work may start from the lower tunnel end (L3).”Medog tunnel exit, close to the Arunachal borderDevelopment began well before the July 2025 groundbreaking.2018: Only one small community was present, but riverside road construction had started.2019-21: Groundwork began, and an industrial and residential site and a bridge were ready by 2021.2023-24: 30-35 new residential and industrial buildings came up.2024: A concrete batching plant was set up between April and August, alongside new bridges, roads, machinery and trucks.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A former mayor of Mississippi’s capital city has been sentenced to 37 months in prison after pleading guilty in a bribery scheme involving a proposed hotel; he must also forfeit $50,000 in property
articles.summary: Former Jackson Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba has been sentenced to 37 months in federal prison for his role in a corruption scheme involving a proposed hotel
articles.body: Former Jackson Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba has been sentenced to 37 months in federal prison for his role in a corruption scheme involving a proposed hotel development in downtown Jackson, Mississippi. According to reports by The Associated Press, Mississippi Today and WLBT, the former mayor was sentenced on November 20, 2026, after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit bribery. He must also forfeit $50,000 in property and serve one year of supervised release after completing his prison term. The case emerged from an FBI undercover operation in which agents posed as real estate developers seeking to build a hotel near Jackson’s downtown convention centre. Investigators alleged that several elected officials accepted money and other benefits in exchange for helping move the proposed development forward. The sentencing marks a major development in a federal corruption investigation that implicated several prominent political figures in Mississippi’s capital.How the FBI uncovered the bribery schemeThe investigation centred on a proposed hotel development near the Jackson Convention Complex. According to the 2024 federal indictment, undercover FBI agents approached local officials while posing as developers interested in securing approval for the project. Prosecutors alleged that Lumumba received $50,000 disguised as campaign contributions in exchange for using his position to help the developers. He was accused of directing a city employee to shorten a bidding deadline, giving the supposed developers an advantage in the process.The operation also involved other senior officials, including former Hinds County District Attorney Jody Owens and former Jackson City Council President Aaron Banks. Federal investigators alleged that the officials worked together to secure support for the development in exchange for payments and other benefits. Lumumba initially maintained his innocence after the charges became public in 2024, describing the prosecution as politically motivated. However, he eventually pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit bribery in July 2026.Other officials were also sentencedThe investigation extended beyond the former mayor, bringing several other political figures and individuals connected to the proposed development under federal scrutiny. Former Hinds County District Attorney Jody Owens and former City Council President Aaron Banks also pleaded guilty to their involvement in the scheme. Both received prison sentences earlier in November. Owens was sentenced to more than three years, while Banks received a sentence of nearly four years.Former City Council Vice President Angelique Lee and businessman Sherik Marve Smith, who was related to Owens, also pleaded guilty to federal bribery charges. The case has drawn considerable attention in Mississippi because of the number of public officials implicated in the investigation and the alleged use of political influence to advance a private development project.A political career ends amid controversyLumumba served two terms as Jackson’s mayor after first winning election in 2017. He was once viewed as a promising young political figure in the Deep South, particularly among Black elected leaders.His political career was also shaped by a series of challenges facing Jackson, including the city’s widely reported water crisis in 2022, which forced state intervention and brought national attention to the condition of its water infrastructure. He lost his re-election campaign in 2025, shortly after the federal charges against him became public.During his sentencing hearing, Lumumba acknowledged the damage his actions had caused to his family and the community he had represented. Federal Judge Daniel P. Jordan III said the case was particularly troubling given the history of political corruption in Jackson and the need for the sentence to discourage similar conduct by other public officials. While the judge acknowledged positive aspects of Lumumba’s character, he ultimately determined that a prison sentence was necessary.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A night carer was disciplined for chatting about Christmas bonuses with colleagues and then got dismissed; a tribunal then ordered her employer to pay her £29,628
articles.summary: A night-time carer in Cornwall has been awarded £29,628 after an employment tribunal ruled that her dismissal from a care home was unfair.
articles.body: A night-time carer in Cornwall has been awarded £29,628 after an employment tribunal ruled that her dismissal from a care home was unfair. Donna Williams, who worked at Copthorne Care Homes in Penzance, faced disciplinary action after discussing changes to Christmas bonuses with colleagues and for not waiting for her shift in a designated area. She was later investigated over several allegations relating to her work and conduct before being dismissed in June 2024. The tribunal found that her employer had failed to establish reasonable grounds for its decision.Why was the night carer disciplined over Christmas bonus discussionsAccording to The Independent, Williams had worked as a night-time care assistant at Copthorne Care Homes since August 2012. Her employment continued after the business changed ownership in 2022, but the new management introduced a different approach to Christmas bonuses.Previously, all employees received an additional payment during the festive season. Under the new ownership, however, bonuses were no longer guaranteed to every member of staff. Instead, the care home operated a system in which employees were rewarded if they were considered to have gone above and beyond their normal duties.The change became a subject of discussion among employees, including Williams. The tribunal heard that staff had spoken about Christmas bonuses every year for approximately 11 years.Following Christmas 2023, Williams was called to an investigatory meeting on January 3, 2024. Three matters were discussed, including leaving a whole swede in a pan without covering it with water, talking to colleagues about Christmas bonuses and not sitting in the side conservatory while waiting for her shift to begin.She attended a disciplinary hearing on January 26 and received a written warning covering all 3 matters. Management also instructed her not to discuss bonuses again and told her to return to waiting in the designated conservatory.What did the tribunal say about the bonus policyThe employment tribunal questioned the care home's decision to treat conversations about bonuses as misconduct. It found that Copthorne Care Homes had not provided evidence showing that employees had previously been instructed not to discuss the payments.The panel also accepted Williams' account that staff members had spoken about the bonuses for around 11 years. It considered that preventing employees from discussing their pay and working conditions went too far, particularly when a Christmas bonus formed part of their employment benefits.The tribunal also examined the other reasons behind the initial warning. Although the care home had raised concerns about food preparation and where Williams waited before starting work, the panel later found that some of the allegations against her were not supported by clear workplace procedures.The Independent reported that the tribunal considered the absence of an established instruction about bonus discussions particularly important. It found no evidence of a policy or procedure governing handovers.The disciplinary action escalated before her dismissalThe situation became more serious in March 2024, when Williams was investigated again over allegations relating to her care duties. She was suspended on full pay on March 19 while the employer examined several complaints about her work.These included allegations that she had failed to replace a service user's pain relief patches, left a woman sitting in a chair throughout the night and had not properly reported a fall.However, the evidence presented to the tribunal raised questions about how these incidents had been handled. In relation to the woman who remained in a chair overnight, a colleague provided evidence that Williams had intended to move the service user after she woke up, as she regularly slept in that position. On this occasion, however, the woman slept throughout the night.Williams also had mobility difficulties because of arthritis, which affected her ability to move the service user. The tribunal was told that the care home had not provided evidence explaining exactly what it expected Williams to do in that situation.The circumstances surrounding the reported fall were also considered. Williams had contacted an ambulance, the service user's next of kin and a colleague after the incident. Despite these details, she received a final written warning on April 4.She appealed against the decision and was subsequently signed off sick. Her absence continued from April 5 until May 6, followed by another period of sickness absence between May 6 and June 10.According to The Independent, Williams returned to work in June but was told not to discuss the earlier disciplinary proceedings with colleagues.What finally led to the care worker losing her jobWilliams' return to work did not bring an end to the disciplinary dispute. She was suspended again on June 19, 2024, over allegations that she had discussed confidential information with colleagues and spoken negatively about a co-worker involved in the disciplinary process.The employer had little evidence to support the charge against her comments. Much of the information was hearsay about conversations that had allegedly taken place at a pub, The Independent said.Williams was released on June 27, 2024. She appealed the decision internally but was rejected by the management of the care home. She then brought an unfair dismissal claim against Copthorne Care Homes at Bodmin Employment Tribunal in Cornwall.The tribunal also considered the chronology of the disciplinary proceedings and found that the employer had seriously mishandled the case. It found that the care home had not demonstrated that it genuinely believed that the alleged misconduct had occurred. It also ruled that management’s actions were not on reasonable grounds.As reported by HR Magazine on November 19, 2026, the tribunal upheld Williams' complaint of unfair dismissal and also found that she was entitled to compensation for wrongful dismissal.How much compensation has the former carer been awardedThe tribunal ordered Copthorne Care Homes to pay Williams a total of £29,628.14. The award included £2,680 in unpaid notice pay, more than £18,000 for financial losses, an additional award of £4,020 and an uplift to the compensation.However, the tribunal did not uphold every part of Williams' case. Her separate claim of disability discrimination was unsuccessful, despite evidence that her arthritis had affected her mobility and ability to carry out certain physical tasks.You use AI every day. articles.title: 22 lakh pleas to include names in West Bengal rolls top priority: SC to EC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday said priority must be given to the appeals of 22 lakh people, of the total 38 lakh, seeking restoration of their names in the West Bengal electoral roll, and sought the state govt's response to allegations that voters deleted during SIR are being denied ration and benefits under various social welfare schemes.The court also said even among the 22 lakh, cases of those from wards in Kolkata Municipal Corporation should be heard ahead of others, keeping in view the upcoming civic elections.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the Calcutta HC chief justice in consultation with Election Commission must increase the number of tribunals - currently 19 - to deal with the 38 lakh appeals, filed on deletion of 90 lakh voters declared absent, shifted, duplicate or dead, or flagged for 'logical discrepancy', related to mapping.The bench also asked Election Commission to requisition additional space for housing the tribunals at various places to facilitate easy access to appellants.SC's direction came after advocate Prashant Bhushan told SC that of the 1.4 lakh appeals decided so far by tribunals, which were appointed to adjudicate a large number of appeals filed after SIR, more than 90% have been allowed leading to restoration of their names in the electoral roll.This is a strong indicator based on a large sample size to persuade the top court to direct that those who have filed appeals against deletion of their names should be allowed to vote in the coming elections, Bhushan said.Supreme Court said this was the reason for it to ask for prioritisation of appeals for restoration of names relating to various wards in KMC.Bhushan, supported by senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan, told the apex court that even though the court had categorically clarified that deletion of names from electoral roll would not have any consequence, including with regard to citizenship, beyond the chance to vote, state govt has been denying the deleted voters ration through public distribution system (PDS) and benefits under social welfare schemes, including Annapurna Yojna.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said these are bald assertions and alleged that the petitioners have not cited a single example to substantiate their claims.However, the CJI-led bench asked state govt to file response to the allegations.In a related issue, SC postponed to Wednesday hearing on state govt's appeal challenging an interim order of a division bench of Calcutta HC restraining the state EC from announcing schedule for KMC polls, in which the number of wards were increased from 144 to 209 by an amending Act. Mehta said the high court mistakenly concluded that state govt lacked the jurisdiction to carry out the exercise of increasing the number of wards and resultant adjustment of ward boundaries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Don't be a Baahubali: SC to Bihar judge over criminal case against SP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An additional sessions judge in Bihar's Sasaram was chastised on Monday by Supreme Court which took exception to him flexing his position and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An additional sessions judge in Bihar's Sasaram was chastised on Monday by Supreme Court which took exception to him flexing his position and getting a criminal case registered against a superintendent of police who did not carry out his order, and asked the judge "not to be Quixotic or play Robin Hood or Baahubali of Bihar".The ASJ, in a criminal trial, had directed the SP to file an FIR against a witness for deposing falsely. After his repeated summons were not complied with, the judge directed the Bihar chief secretary to take disciplinary action against the SP.When that did not work, the ASJ directed a criminal case against the SP and asked him to appear in court Aug 22. After two adjournments, the SP's counsel sought permission for virtual appearance on the grounds that he was supervising flood relief.In the meantime, the inspecting judge from the HC asked the sessions judge to meet him with the case records in Patna on Sept 24, which the judicial officer declined saying "it was very humiliating and demoralising" for him. On Sept 29, the sessions judge convicted the SP for flouting court orders and fined him Re 1.On the state govt's appeal, Patna HC criticised the judicial officer's conduct and asked him to be circumspect and exercise caution in future. Hurt by these remarks, the judicial officer appealed against the HC judgment before the SC and said, "The present case depicts the pitiable plight of judicial officers once they pass any order against an IAS or IPS officer. The entire system tends to protect them, leaving judicial officers high and dry."A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said every judge was bound by procedure and asked if a district judge could behave like this? "When an inspecting judge asks you to meet him, why would you not go?" the bench asked."Every judge must know the contours of his jurisdiction. Don't be Quixotic or a Robin Hood," the bench said and asked the judicial officer's counsel Prem Prakash to convey to him not "to become Baahubali of Bihar".The bench said in its order, "Regardless of the observations made by the HC in its Oct 8 order, we request the HC to consider petitioner judicial officer's explanation-cum-apology sympathetically and dispose of the pending proceedings."On another judicial officer's petition complaining about promotion and selection to higher judicial service, the CJI-led bench said, "It has become a fashion for judicial officers to rush to the SC directly without approaching the HCs concerned. They are thinking 24x7 about promotion, increase in salary and perks and extension of retirement age, paying little attention to deal with huge pendency."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A woman underwent a breast MRI in 2019, but doctors allegedly missed an incidental lung cancer finding; seven years later, a jury awarded nearly $8 million in a medical negligence case.
articles.summary: A medical negligence case in Oregon has ended with a jury awarding nearly $8 million to the family of a woman whose lung cancer was allegedly overlooked
articles.body: A medical negligence case in Oregon has ended with a jury awarding nearly $8 million to the family of a woman whose lung cancer was allegedly overlooked during a breast MRI. The scan was performed in 2019, but the abnormality in her lung was not identified until she returned for another examination the following year. By then, the cancer had spread to her lymph nodes.The case concerned Wendi K. Lui, who underwent regular breast cancer screening because she was considered at higher risk. According to healthcare trade publication Radiology Business, in April 2019, Lui visited Legacy Good Samaritan for an MRI as part of her annual screening. She also underwent mammography.The radiologist reviewing the images, Kari A. Thomas of Diagnostic Imaging NW, found no suspicious signs of breast cancer. However, the legal claim brought by Lui's family centred on another part of the scan. They argued that an abnormal mass in her lung was visible but was not reported or referred for further examination.The significance of that finding emerged more than a year later. During a second breast MRI in June 2020, another radiologist noticed a mass in Lui's left lung and advised additional testing. A PET scan in July confirmed non-small cell lung cancer. Lui had never smoked, according to the report.She later developed metastatic lung cancer and died on December 6, 2023, aged 51. Her husband, Gene Lui, subsequently took legal action against the healthcare providers involved in her treatment. On November 9, after an 11-day trial, a Multnomah County jury awarded nearly $8 million to her estate and husband.How the lung abnormality went undetectedThe family's case also involved earlier imaging records that showed the lung mass had been present for some time. Lui first underwent a breast MRI in 2018, aged 46. She had dense breast tissue, which can make it more difficult to identify abnormalities during breast imaging.According to the report, the lung mass measured approximately 1 centimetre in 2018. It had increased to around 2 centimetres by the time of her April 2019 examination. Despite the change, the finding was not flagged for further investigation during that scan.When Lui returned in June 2020, radiologist Sam Gruner of Diagnostic Imaging NW identified the mass in her left lung. He recommended a CT scan to examine it further. Subsequent PET imaging confirmed the cancer diagnosis.The delay meant that the disease had reached her lymph nodes before it was detected. The family's legal argument was that the earlier scan should have prompted additional medical checks.Husband wanted the case heard in courtGene Lui pursued the legal battle after his wife's death. His background as a psychiatrist and his previous employment with Legacy Health System helped him examine the medical care she had received, The Oregonian reported.He filed the lawsuit in 2024. However, the case had a limitation because the 2018 scan fell outside the applicable statute of limitations. The legal claim therefore focused on the radiologist's interpretation of the April 2019 examination.The defence questioned whether the radiology group could be held liable for failing to identify the mass. Its lawyer, Mike Wiswall, argued that the assessment had to be based on what a radiologist could reasonably have recognised at the time, without knowing that Lui would later be diagnosed with cancer."The issue at trial was whether a careful radiologist interpreting the 2019 MRI, without knowledge of the later diagnosis, should have flagged that area for further evaluation," Wiswall said in a statement to local media.Gene Lui also faced the option of settling the dispute before trial. The healthcare providers had reportedly made several settlement offers, but he declined them. He wanted the circumstances surrounding his wife's diagnosis to be examined publicly rather than resolved through a private agreement. "From the beginning, I was hell-bent to get this to a trial," he told The Oregonian.Explaining his decision, he said he was concerned that a settlement could allow the providers to avoid acknowledging any wrongdoing."Because if this got settled, these people who I used to work for would say, ‘We didn’t do anything wrong.’ And nothing will ever change," he said.Rachel O'Neal, the lawyer representing the family, said the decision was not simply about securing financial compensation. She said Gene wanted the case to receive public attention and explain what had happened to his wife."There was no sum of money that was worth sweeping it under the rug. … Gene wanted to be able to tell his story. He wanted to be interviewed by the press. He wanted people to know what happened," O'Neal told The Oregonian.Verdict highlights importance of incidental findingsFollowing the verdict, O'Neal said the case should encourage radiologists to examine all the structures visible on imaging scans, rather than concentrating only on the area mentioned in the examination request.She said breast MRI examinations also require attention to structures inside the chest because they can reveal abnormalities unrelated to breast cancer."We hope this verdict brings awareness to the importance of radiologists evaluating the intrathoracic structures on breast MRIs. Radiologists need a systematic process that ensures they review everything on the images," she told Radiology Business.O'Neal added that identifying an abnormality is essential before it can be reported and investigated. "Incidental extra-mammary findings must be reported, and they cannot be reported if no one looks for them. The jury applied that standard here," she said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russia planning to launch N-arms into space?
articles.summary: Nato chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to
articles.body: Nato chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Public broadcasters WDR and NDR, along with the Sueddeutsche Zeitung daily, reported that Russia planned to launch a satellite dubbed "Sputnik-S" equipped with a nuclear warhead sometime in the coming weeks.The outlets, citing unnamed sources, said that the intelligence reports about the plans had recently been shared among several Nato countries and that the German govt had been briefed on the matter. The satellite had been stored in the Moscow region, according to the news outlets, and could be used to disrupt or destroy important communications and observation satellites orbiting Earth. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the latest news stories on the topic but that frequent reports citing "unknown sources" are "hardly worth taking seriously".(This is an AFP story)You use AI every day. articles.title: A New York family kept building a winter ice rink in its front yard despite $100 weekly HOA fines; a judge ruled the ban invalid and cancelled nearly $2,000 in penalties
articles.summary: A family in Clarence, New York, can keep building an ice rink in its front yard.
articles.body: A family in Clarence, New York, can keep building an ice rink in its front yard. The Zinnos skated for a year before their homeowners' association prohibited ice rinks in all front yards. They continued to erect one in each of the next two years, and the association began levying weekly fines of $100, reaching approximately $2,000. On 6 January 2026, Justice Peter Allen Weinmann of the Supreme Court, Erie County, declared the ban invalid and ruled the fines null and void, finding the board had skipped the 67% homeowner vote its Declaration required.New York family’s front-yard ice rink sparks a $2,000 HOA fine disputeAccording to the ruling in Zinno v. Waterford Village Association, Inc., the Zinnos enjoyed a carefree year of ice skating before their HOA decided to prohibit ice rinks in all front yards. The family continued to erect a rink in each of the next two years. The HOA then began levying weekly fines of $100, and the balance had reached approximately $2,000 by the time of the decision.The ruling states that the Zinnos sued the association, alleging violations of the HOA's governing rules. The HOA countersued, also alleging violations of those rules, and sought to collect the outstanding fines. According to the court, both sides' counsel agreed at oral argument that no facts were in dispute, and that the issue was a question of law, so both sought summary judgment.HOA rules did not originally prohibit front-yard ice rinksThe decision describes the central issue as a conflict between two documents: the Declaration of Protective Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions, Easements, Charges and Liens, and the Architectural and Maintenance Standards and Guidelines. The Declaration was created in 2004 by the developer. It runs to 15 articles, schedules and exhibits across almost 60 pages. The judge wrote that it "functions as a constitution" and forms part of the deed to every property in the association, which counsel put at approximately 100.According to the ruling, Article X of the Declaration sets rules on almost 20 topics, including signs, animals, fences and walls, garbage, hunting, above-ground swimming pools, exterior storage, open fires, trees, and snowmobiles, motorcycles and ATVs; it contains no reference to ice rinks. The Architectural Guidelines were issued in 2014 by the Architectural Committee, which the board of directors was empowered to create under Article VIII. They span 14 pages and cover approximately 15 topics, such as fences, exterior storage sheds, play sets, pools, fire pits and solar panels, and they also do not mention ice rinks. The decision records that in 2022, after the Zinnos erected a rink in their front yard, the committee issued revised guidelines that addressed ice rinks and required them to be placed only in backyards, among other restrictions.Judge says HOA needed homeowners’ approval to ban ice rinksThe court framed the question as whether the board had to follow the Declaration's amendment procedure, or could restrict ice rinks by amending the Architectural Guidelines by a majority vote of the board. According to the ruling, Article XI allows an amendment to be proposed by the board or by a petition of not less than 25% of lot owners. After notice and a hearing, it must be approved by 67% or more of lot owners.The judge pointed to two Appellate Division cases. In Turon v. Meadowbrook Pointe HOA, Inc., a board rule barred dogs over 25 lbs although the governing documents were silent on dog size, and the court sided with the homeowner. In Board of Managers of Village View Condominium v. Forman, a board rule banned all pets where the governing documents did not address the issue, and the court invalidated it for breaching the required 80% owner approval. The decision also cites case law holding that ambiguity in a restrictive covenant is construed against the drafter, and that where language supports two equally plausible readings, the less restrictive reading is adopted. According to the ruling, the party seeking to enforce a covenant carries the burden of proof.Judge voids ice rink ban and nearly $2,000 in HOA finesAccording to the court, there was no ambiguity: altering the restrictions listed in Article X required approval by 67% of all homeowners at a duly noticed meeting, and that did not happen. The judge described the Architectural Guidelines as a subsidiary set of regulations whose authority was created by the Declaration, and wrote that the board's action amended the Declaration without the required vote. The court also held that the business judgment rule, which limits judicial review of authorised board decisions, did not protect the rule because the board's action was authorised by the Declaration.The decision declares the HOA's prohibition on front-yard ice rinks invalid and rules the accumulated fines against the Zinnos null and void. It states that if the HOA wishes to regulate ice rinks, it must schedule a duly noticed vote of all homeowners, which would require 67% approval to pass. The judge directed the plaintiffs' counsel to submit an order on notice within 30 days. The opinion carries a note that it is uncorrected and will not be published in the printed Official Reports.Disclaimer: This article is based on the publicly available decision in Zinno v Waterford Village Association, Inc. (2026 NY Slip Op 50137(U)), published by the New York State Law Reporting Bureau. The Times of India has not independently verified the details of the dispute, the fines levied, the association's rules or the circumstances mentioned. The decision is marked as uncorrected and will not be published in the printed Official Reports. The information should not be interpreted as confirmation from the Zinno family, Waterford Village Association, Inc. or their representatives, and it is not legal advice.You use AI every day. articles.title: Alice had contact with China spy agency during affair: Report
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: Drowned out in the rapture among Jensen Huang's fan club over his return after US President Donald Trump's intervention
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Drowned out in the rapture among Jensen Huang's fan club over his return after US President Donald Trump's intervention were leaks from the American intelligence community that Alice Huang, the Chinese woman Jensen Huang had an affair with, kept in contact with an official of China's top spy agency for more than a year during her dalliance with the Nvidia boss. US intelligence agencies also gathered evidence that Ms Huang's business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency, according to media reports.All that hardly seemed to matter as America's tech elite lined up behind Trump to force Huang's return.Elon Musk, who had even suggested that hiring Huang at one of his own companies would be an honour, while others had urged him to either start a new company or join a rival, declared after the reinstatement, "The mistake has been corrected." The White House made no secret of Trump's intervention, calling the Nvidia board's reversal "a great decision" and echoing Trump's words that "we have to protect our geniuses."Indeed, Trump himself had to untangle the conflict within the administration after Huang's exit appeared to have been forced by China hardliners like Marco Rubio, who reportedly strengthened the language suggesting he was honeytrapped in a Chinese spying operation. But pro-business voices like commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and pro-tech spokespersons like former Trump AI advisor David Sacks questioned the allegations against Huang, arguing that he was being forced out before the facts had been established.Trump, who always seemed to have a sympathetic ear for Huang, went with the latter group. "The US Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct," he said in a post on Truth Social, adding, "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure."Not everyone was thrilled by the board turnaround after Trump intervention which takes presidential influence in corporate America to a new level. Senator Elizabeth Warren was among the critics, calling the reinstatement reckless while demanding that Nvidia's leadership answer questions about export-control compliance. She also asked the Trump administration to disclose which senior officials had advised the board that Huang's return posed no national security risk even as reports continued to filter out about Alice Huang's ties to Beijing and Jensen Huang's own intemperate behavior with his associates and subordinates at Nvidia.Indeed, as if the intelligence concerns were not damaging enough, separate disclosures painted a decidedly less flattering portrait of Huang's management style. A NYT investigation drawing on interviews with more than a dozen current and former employees and two decades of documents and court records, described a corporate culture in which humiliation and intimidation were routinely deployed as management tools at Nvidia.Huang's alleged outbursts were extraordinary. He reportedly told one executive that his mother should have aborted him, threatened to beat a subordinate with the person's own arms and told another that he would tear off the top of his head and urinate on his brain. In one disturbing account, he reportedly described humiliation as a way of extracting greater performance from employees who had become too wealthy to be motivated by money. The behaviour had generated workplace complaints and, in at least two cases, confidential settlements with former senior executives, according to the NYT.Yet it also described a company where Huang inspired extraordinary devotion. The devotion expressed itself in an online campaign, dubbed 'Stand with Jensen', which attracted more than 194,000 signatures at its peak.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: "Main problem is not money; it's how to...": CA explains how to invest Rs 5 lakh in stocks, gold, FDs and bonds to build wealth and minimise risk
articles.summary: Receiving Rs 5 lakh at once can feel like an opportunity to finally make a meaningful financial move. But the bigger question is what to do with the money.
articles.body: Receiving Rs 5 lakh at once can feel like an opportunity to finally make a meaningful financial move. But the bigger question is what to do with the money. Put it in the stock market, keep it in a fixed deposit, buy gold or spread it across different investment options?Chartered Accountant and content creator Srishti Gosavi recently addressed this question by sharing how she would invest Rs 5 lakh if she had the money available today. Rather than putting the entire amount into one asset, she suggested dividing it across different financial instruments, balancing potential growth with stability and income.Her approach takes into account factors such as age, financial responsibilities, risk appetite and whether someone already has an emergency fund. She also made it clear that her allocation was a personal investment approach, not a universal formula everyone should follow.Start with growth, but don't put everything into equityFor someone below 50 years of age without specific dependents, Gosavi said she would consider allocating around 40 to 50 per cent of the money to equity. That would mean investing approximately Rs 2 lakh to Rs 2.5 lakh in stocks or mutual funds. Equity investments can offer the potential for long-term wealth creation, but they also come with market fluctuations and the possibility of losses. For people who are new to investing and do not know how to evaluate individual stocks, she suggested index funds as an option.Index funds track a market index and allow investors to participate in a broad group of companies rather than depending on the performance of a single stock. However, they are still market-linked investments and can fall in value, particularly over shorter periods. The idea behind this portion of her portfolio is to give some of the money an opportunity to grow over time, instead of keeping the entire amount in instruments that may offer relatively lower returns.A four-part plan for Rs 5 lakhRather than treating the money as one lump sum, Gosavi's approach divides it into different roles. Each portion is meant to serve a separate purpose, from long-term growth to safer savings and income generation. The following is her suggested allocation, not a personalised investment recommendation.She would allocate 40 to 50% (Rs 2 lakh to Rs 2.5 lakh) towards equity, investing in stocks, mutual funds or index funds for long-term growth. Another 10 to 20% (Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh) would go into safer investments such as fixed deposits, arbitrage funds or debt mutual funds, particularly if she did not already have an emergency fund. She would also set aside 10 to 20% (Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh) for gold, preferring gold ETFs, gold stocks or gold mutual funds over jewellery. The remaining 10 to 20% (Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh) would be invested in income-generating instruments, such as bonds and non-convertible debentures (NCDs), which can provide periodic income.Bonds or non-convertible debentures (NCDs) that may provide periodic income. The percentages are indicative ranges and are not meant to be applied mechanically. The allocation should be adjusted to suit individual circumstances.Why she says this is not a magic formulaGosavi was clear that her strategy should not be blindly copied by everyone. A person carrying loans, lacking emergency savings or needing the money in the near future would have a very different investment priority from someone with stable finances and a longer time horizon. She explained, "This is not a magic formula for 5 lakh rupees of investment. This is dependent on my risk appetite." She also stressed that she would remain invested for at least five years, making the investment horizon an important part of her decision.Her closing message was, "It's about putting the right amount of money at the right place for the right time." The idea is that investing is not simply about chasing returns or choosing the most popular financial product. It involves understanding when the money may be needed, how much risk one can tolerate and whether the portfolio is aligned with personal goals.The internet's takeaway: earning is only half the jobHer investment breakdown also prompted conversations about financial discipline, managing money wisely and building wealth with a purpose. While some users appreciated the simplicity of her explanation, others were interested in learning more about bonds and non-convertible debentures.One user commented: "Absolutely—earning money is one part, but knowing how to manage, invest, and spend it wisely makes the real difference." Another wrote, "A strong perspective on making money work with purpose." A third user thanked her for simplifying the approach, writing, "Thank you for sharing this valuable information. The way you explained is amazing."The larger takeaway from Gosavi's video is that having money to invest is only the beginning. Knowing how to divide it, understanding the risks and giving investments enough time can be equally important. Her approach encourages people to think beyond a single investment option and build a financial plan around their own needs, rather than following someone else's portfolio without understanding it.You use AI every day. articles.title: 5.4 magnitude earthquake jolts Nepal; tremors felt across parts of eastern India
articles.summary: A magnitude 5.4 earthquake struck Nepal’s Koshi Province early Tuesday morning, triggering tremors across parts of eastern and northeastern India, Bhutan
articles.body: A magnitude 5.4 earthquake struck Nepal’s Koshi Province early Tuesday morning, triggering tremors across parts of eastern and northeastern India, Bhutan and Bangladesh. Reports of shaking also emerged from parts of China, with residents in several areas experiencing the impact of the early-morning quake.The earthquake struck near Lelep in Nepal’s Koshi Province at around 7:02 am IST, according to initial reports from the United States Geological Survey (USGS). The National Centre for Seismology (NCS), meanwhile, recorded the tremor at magnitude 5.3, with its epicentre located at latitude 27.855°N and longitude 87.909°E, at a depth of 20 kilometres.Tremors were reported across parts of eastern and northeastern India, including Bihar, Meghalaya and North Bengal, as well as areas bordering the Himalayan region.Initial estimates from the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC), cited by Reuters, also placed the earthquake at magnitude 5.3, with a reported depth of around 10 kilometres.Separately, a magnitude 2.5 earthquake struck Assam’s Karbi Anglong district at 3:39 am on Tuesday. According to the NCS, the quake occurred at a depth of 15 kilometres, with its epicentre at latitude 25.743°N and longitude 93.355°E.Meanwhile, another earthquake was reported in Pakistan, near the Sindh-Balochistan border. The tremor was recorded at a depth of 17 kilometres, according to preliminary information.Further details on the impact of the earthquakes are awaited.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Saryu-Kamala Express service initially open only to Indian, Nepalese nationals
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: The newly inaugurated Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, will initially be open only to
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The newly inaugurated Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, will initially be open only to Indian and Nepalese nationals, as the Bureau of Immigration (BoI) does not have an operational immigration clearance facility at Jaynagar railway station in Bihar’s Madhubani district, the last Indian stop before the train crosses into Nepal.The weekly international train service, virtually inaugurated on Monday by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah, is scheduled to begin commercial operations on November 28.However, ticket bookings have yet to open on the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) website or at railway passenger reservation system (PRS) counters.A senior officer of the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) confirmed that the absence of an immigration clearance facility at Jaynagar would prevent passengers from countries other than India and Nepal from travelling on the train.“There is no immigration clearance facility at Jaynagar. Once it becomes operational, the Railways may allow ticket bookings for foreign nationals. Currently, no one other than the citizens of India and Nepal can travel on this train,” said Rajendra Singh, commandant of the SSB's 48th Battalion at Jaynagar, which is responsible for border movement checks.The officer said SSB personnel would continue checking passengers' credentials when the train reaches Jaynagar. In Bihar, there are two immigration checking points, one at Raxaul in East Champaran district and the other at Jogbani in Araria district.Although Indian and Nepalese nationals enjoy special cross-border travel arrangements under existing bilateral agreements, passengers from other countries require immigration clearance to cross the international border.Notably, the Railway Board has provided for a two-hour scheduled halt at Jaynagar for the train travelling from Ayodhya to Janakpur Dham and a one-hour halt in the opposite direction.According to the Railway Board, the service will operate as trains numbered 15595 and 15596, named the Janakpur Dham-Ayodhya Cantt Express.Train number 15595 will depart from Janakpur Dham every Saturday at 1.10pm Nepal time and reach Jaynagar at 2.10pm Indian Standard Time (IST). After a one-hour halt, it will depart at 3.10pm IST.The train will reach Sitamarhi at 7pm, Narkatiaganj at 10.50pm and Gorakhpur at 3.55am before reaching Ayodhya Cantt at 8.10am on Sunday.Train number 15596 will depart from Ayodhya Cantt every Monday at 5.50pm and reach Gorakhpur at 10.13pm. It will subsequently reach Narkatiaganj at 1.50am and Sitamarhi at 4.42am on Tuesday.The train will reach Jaynagar at 8.30am IST on Tuesday, where it will halt for two hours before departing at 10.30am IST and reaching Janakpur Dham at 12.40pm Nepal time.The Railway Board has approved commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham.The train will operate with a 17-coach Linke-Hofmann-Busch (LHB) rake, with a total passenger capacity of 1,158. The composition includes eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper coaches, one seating coach and one power car.Jaynagar will serve as the primary maintenance station, while watering facilities will be available at Narkatiaganj and Gorakhpur. articles.title: 10 arrested for luring SC families to convert to Christianity with money in Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Amethi police arrested 10 people, including four women, on Monday for allegedly persuading Scheduled Caste families to convert to Christianity by
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Amethi police arrested 10 people, including four women, on Monday for allegedly persuading Scheduled Caste families to convert to Christianity by promising financial aid, free medical treatment and educational support at religious gatherings in Sindurwa village under Kamrauli police station.Police said prayer meetings were held at Raj Kumar alias Joel's home, where locals spotted 20-25 people. Police arrested the accused and recovered four books related to religious conversion. The group allegedly used a church network and influenced nearly 240 people over six years, organising meetings across Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand, Odisha and Tamil Nadu. Investigators are examining suspected cash funding, possible tax evasion and Maharashtra church links. Police said Srinivasan Iyengar, alias Daniel, handled the group's finances.A case was registered under Sections 3 and 5(1) of the UP Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act. Those arrested were Raj Kumar, Srinivasan Daniel, Royal Rodrigues, Mahipal Singh Bind, Prakash Rao, Kanhaiya Bind, Suryakala, Divya Daniel, Rita Rodrigues and Elvina Williams. articles.title: New Haven agrees to pay $30 million to George Gould, who spent nearly 27 years in prison, and the estate of Ronald Taylor, who died in 2011, after their convictions in a 1993 murder were thrown out
articles.summary: Nearly three decades behind bars, a conviction that unravelled years later and a settlement worth millions of dollars have brought two wrongful-conviction
articles.body: Nearly three decades behind bars, a conviction that unravelled years later and a settlement worth millions of dollars have brought two wrongful-conviction cases in Connecticut closer to a conclusion. The city of New Haven has agreed to pay $30 million to George Gould and the estate of Ronald Taylor, who were imprisoned for a 1993 murder they did not commit. While Gould will receive $18 million after spending almost 27 years incarcerated, Taylor's estate is set to receive $12 million following his death in 2011. The settlement, reported by the New Haven Independent and Hartford Courant, marks another major financial resolution for the city as it faces mounting lawsuits linked to wrongful convictions dating back several decades.Two men convicted in a 1993 murderGould and Taylor were convicted of felony murder and other charges in connection with the July 4, 1993, killing of Eugenia Vega inside her Grand Avenue bodega in New Haven.According to the New Haven Independent, the prosecution's case relied heavily on testimony from a woman who claimed to have witnessed the crime. She later revealed that she had been arrested for prostitution and interrogated while experiencing severe heroin withdrawal. She alleged that police offered to help her obtain heroin in exchange for providing the statement they wanted. Investigators reportedly found no physical evidence linking either Gould or Taylor to the killing.Years later, two relatives reportedly approached the FBI and said Vega's son had confessed to them that he had killed his father, bringing fresh scrutiny to the convictions.A lengthy legal battle before exonerationThe men's legal struggle involved multiple court proceedings. In 2010, a Connecticut Superior Court judge granted their habeas corpus petitions on grounds of actual innocence and ordered their release.However, the state appealed, and the Connecticut Supreme Court subsequently overturned that decision. During a second habeas proceeding, their petitions were denied, the online report adds.Gould returned to prison in 2011, while Taylor was allowed to remain at home because of his terminal cancer diagnosis. He died in October 2011, after spending more than 16 years incarcerated, New Haven Independent reported.Gould continued challenging his conviction and was released in 2021 after a judge modified his sentence. The state's Conviction Integrity Unit later reviewed the case, and prosecutors moved to vacate both convictions in 2024.$30 million settlement and approval processThe agreement was reached on November 13 in two consolidated federal civil rights cases against the city, the report added.Under the settlement, Gould will receive $18 million, while Taylor's estate, administered by Mary Murphy-Taylor, will receive $12 million. The latter payment remains subject to approval by the New Haven Probate Court.According to the Hartford Courant, the agreement also requires approval from the city's Litigation Settlement Committee. The New Haven Board of Alders must subsequently approve borrowing for the settlement.The New Haven Independent reported that Gould's legal representatives include Neufeld Scheck Brustin Hoffmann & Freudenberger, the Law Offices of Richard Emanuel and the Law Office of Attorney Michael A. Jefferson.Wrongful-conviction settlements reach $77 millionThe latest agreement represents the fourth and fifth federal civil rights lawsuits New Haven has settled within three months. Earlier settlements involved Adam Carmon for $16.5 million, Vernon Horn for $15.25 million and Marquis Jackson for $15.25 million.Together, the five settlements total $77 million. According to city officials cited by the New Haven Independent and Hartford Courant, borrowing to finance the payments could result in at least $116 million in repayments over 20 years when interest is included.Mayor Justin Elicker has acknowledged the city's responsibility to address past injustices while raising concerns about the financial burden on taxpayers. He has also called for the state to share more of the costs, noting that state authorities appealed the original decision granting Gould and Taylor relief.The mayor's office has pointed to the city's lack of insurance coverage for this type of incident in 1993 and the financial implications of settling claims decades later.More lawsuits remain unresolvedThe financial consequences may not end with the latest agreement. According to the New Haven Independent, lawsuits involving former Alder Troy Streater and Charles Coleman Jr. remain outstanding, alongside the separate case involving Stefon Morant, in which a jury previously awarded $38 million against the city. New Haven is appealing that verdict.For Gould, the settlement brings an end to a legal struggle that continued long after his release. articles.title: Wars choke global food routes, threatening aid for 7.3 million, WFP warns
articles.summary: WFP Executive Director Luke Lindberg decries ‘political problem’ as grain is ‘not reaching the people who need it’.
articles.body:
The head of the World Food Programme (WFP) has warned that disruption to three critical trade routes is pushing up food and humanitarian costs, threatening assistance to millions of people.

Addressing the United Nations Security Council in New York on Monday, WFP Executive Director Luke Lindberg said a “triple chokepoint” in the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandeb and the Black Sea had “dramatically tightened the supply of food exports and farming inputs”.

“Combined with a surge in conflicts and climate shocks like El Nino, the effect on food production and prices has been very real,” he said.

If current conditions persist, the agency expects $727m in additional costs by mid-2027, potentially putting assistance for 7.3 million people at risk.

“This is taking money straight out of WFP’s operations, directly translating into less food for fewer families,” Lindberg said.

The warning comes as 266 million people worldwide face acute hunger, with a risk of famine in parts of Sudan, South Sudan and Somalia.

About 30 percent of global fertiliser supplies pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The Black Sea is a key source of grain for countries including Somalia and Yemen, which imports 90 percent of its food.

By mid-October, 63 percent fewer wheat and maize vessels were moving through the Bosphorus than a year earlier, the WFP said. About 10 million tonnes of Russian and Ukrainian wheat could fail to reach global markets, enough to feed an estimated 44 million people.

“This is not a problem of production. It is a political problem,” Lindberg said. “Grain is available, but it is not reaching the people who need it.”

In Sudan, the cost of a basic diet has risen by 130 percent since February.

Lindberg urged member states to commit to three “red lines”: no more famines, no more weaponisation of food and no more attacks on humanitarians.

articles.title: Warning for crashing waves on Isle of Man coastal roads
articles.summary: Ronaldsway Met Office warns of strong winds at high tide bringing debris ashore on exposed roads.
articles.body:
Drivers have been warned of large waves crashing onto exposed coastal roads at high tide in several parts of the Isle of Man.

An amber weather warning has been put in place until 12:30 GMT, with Douglas, Laxey, Ramsey, and Castletown promenades, as well as Shore Road in Gansey, likely to be affected.

Ronaldsway Met Office said gusts of up to 50mph (72km/h), coupled with the spring high tide at around 10:30, was likely to bring debris ashore.

A yellow warning for heavy rain is also in place until midnight, with up to 1.2in (3cm) of rainfall expected to lead to some flooding due to the already saturated ground.
